ROADMAP ON PUMPED STORAGE PROJECTS 
 
707.  SHRI SUBBARAYAN K:  
COM. SELVARAJ V:  
 
Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has brought out a roadmap 
on Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) revealing that the progress in translating the 
pumped storage potential into commissioned capacity has been uneven and slow; 
and  
 
(b)  if so, the details of the bottlenecks identified in the execution of such 
projects and the remedial measures proposed to be taken in this regard? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has prepared a roadmap to achieve 
100 GW of Pumped Storage Project (PSPs) capacity addition by 2035 -36. The 
roadmap presents a comprehensive assessment of the current status of pumped 
storage development in the country, State -wise assessed potential, and the 
projected capacity addition trajectory up to 2035 -36, keeping in view the 
increasing penetration of Variable Renewable Energies (V REs) and the 
corresponding need for long duration storage. The report also outlines key policy, 
regulatory and institutional measures required for expeditious development and 
improved viability of PSPs, including aspects related to project clearances, 
transmission planning, and manufacturing preparedness. 
 
(b) : The development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) is impacted by various 
challenges including difficulties in carrying out survey and investigation activities 
in forest areas, issues related to land acquisition, Re habilitation and 
Resettlement (R&R), Eco-Sensitive Zones, high initial capital costs, and delays in 
the creation of essential infrastructure.  To address these challenges and 
facilitate accelerated development of PSPs, the follo wing measures have been 
taken: 
 
(i) Ministry of Power (MoP) has notified Guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023. 
…….2. 

- 2 - 
 
(ii) Budgetary Support towards Co st of Enabling Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure and 
transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point. 
 
(iii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based on 
open c ompetitive bidding with appropriate risk -sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025, has notified 
tariff based competitive bidding (TBCB) guidelines for procurement of storage 
capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter -State Transmission 
System (ISTS) charges for Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) for a period of 25 
years from the  Commercial Operation Date (COD), in respect of projects for 
which the construction work is awarded on or before 30.06.2028. 
 
(v) The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up hydro 
generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the CEA. 
Further, the Government has exempted off -stream closed -loop pumped 
storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum of capital expenditure, from the 
requirement of concurrence by the CEA. 
 
(vi) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has revised Guidelines for formulation and 
concurrence of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the revised 
guidelines, the timeline for concurrence of DPR has been reduced from 90 
days to 50 days for PSPs. Further, the clearance of Inter-State Aspects is not 
required for PSPs. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2 
category subject to certain conditions.   
 
(viii) The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline 
data for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream closed 
loop PSPs and collection of baseline data for two seasons (pre -monsoon & 
post-monsoon) is prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs. 
 
(ix) The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the provisions relating to survey 
in the forest areas for mining projects to other development projects including 
hydel/PSPs.  
 
(x) MOEF&CC vide letter dated 10.09.2025  has enhanced the number of 
boreholes for undertaking survey and explorations in the forest area for 
mining and developmental projects including hydel / PSPs.

Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to promote the adoption of 
Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) in the civil aviation sector during 2026 and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the policy or regulatory framework formulated for the production, 
certification and use of SAF in the country; 
 
(c) whether any pilot projects or initiatives have been undertaken with airlines, 
airports or oil companies for SAF integration and if so, the details thereof; 
 

(d) the roadmap prepared for scaling up SAF adoption in commercial aviation 
sector and reducing carbon emissions including the targets or timelines fixed in 
this regard; 
 
(e) whether any SAF -related production facilities, research initiatives, 
investment proposals or skill development programmes have been planned or 
implemented in Haryana, particularly in Bhiwani -Mahendergarh Lok Sabha 
Constituency and if so, the details thereof; and

ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): The Government has taken several  steps to support the development 
of a Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) ecosystem in the country. These include: 
(i) Recognition of the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies 
(NABCB) for accreditation of SAF certification bodies under the Int ernational 
Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) scheme, 
(ii) Facilitation of long -term SAF supply arrangements between Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) and airlines, including the signing of Memoranda of 
Understanding between OMCs and Airlines, 
(iii) Support for setting up pilot and commercial -scale SAF production facilities 
under Pradhan Mantri Jaiv Indhan-Vatavaran Anukool Fasal Awashesh Nivaran 
(PM JI-VAN) Yojana, 
(iv) Conducting stakeholder consultations and awareness programmes on SAF. 
Indian O il Corporation limited (IOCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation

for International Aviation (ISCC CORSIA) certification for SAF production at 
their Panipat and Mumbai refineries, respec tively. Further, in June 2026, 
financial assistance was approved under the PM JI -VAN Yojana for three 
commercial-scale and two demonstration-scale SAF projects. 
 
To advance SAF use, Indian carriers have operated following trial flights with 
blends of SAF with traditional Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF): 
 
i. M/s Vistara operated ferry flight of B -787 from USA to India using 28% of

ii. M/s Air Asia operated first commercial domestic flight (Pune to Delhi) with 
0.75% SAF blended fuel on 19th May 2023; 

iii. M/s Spicejet flight operated with 25% SAF (Biofuel produced by Indian 
Institute of Petroleum, CSIR lab) blended with ATF from Dehr adun to Delhi in 
August, 2018. 
 
Further, all Airbus ferry flights fly on 5% SAF blended fuel from Toulouse to 
India. 
 
The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% 
by 2028, and 5% by 2030 for SAF in conventional Aviation Turbine Fuel for 
international operations. Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively 
engaged in achieving the stated blending targets. 
 
(e): IOCL is engaged in the production of SAF at its Panipat Refinery in 
Haryana using Used Cooking Oil (UCO) as feedstock. Further, under the PM JI-
VAN Yojana 2019, amended in 2024, Government provides financial assistance 
for setting up Advanced Biofuels projects including SAF

entries.t: Threat to the Existence of Geruwa River in Bahraich District
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 709 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
THREAT TO THE EXISTENCE OF GERUWA RIVER IN BAHRAICH DISTRICT 
†709.  Dr. ANAND KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasi ng silt deposition, reducing depth and the conseque nt 
threat to the very existence of the Geruwa river in Bahraich district and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is also aware that prote cted aquatic species such as the Ganges river dolph ins, 
crocodiles and gharials are found in the Geruwa riv er and are being adversely affected by the degradat ion of 
the river and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any study/survey has been conducted reg arding the causes of silt deposition in the river, 
particularly deforestation in the upper catchment areas and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the concrete steps being taken by the Governmen t for the conservation of the Geruwa river, desilta tion, 
forest conservation and protection of aquatic biodiversity? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a)    Erosion, movement and deposition of sediment are  natural geo-morphic processes in rivers. Rivers te nd 
to maintain a balance between the silt load carried  and the silt load deposited, thereby maintaining a  river 
regime. The entire Geruwa River, located upstream o f the Girija Barrage, falls under the Katarnia Ghat  
Wildlife Sanctuary. The Government of Uttar Pradesh  has informed that due to reduced flow in the Geruw a 
River, the water velocity decreases, leading to the accumulation of silt in the river bed.  
(b) to (d)    Under the Namami Gange Programme, the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun conducted a 
biodiversity survey of the Geruwa River in January 2023, during which the presence of the Gangetic Dol phin 
(Platanista gangetica ) and Gharial ( Gavialis gangeticus ) was recorded. Gharials of different size classes,  
including nesting females, were observed, indicatin g the presence of a breeding population in the Kata rnia 
Ghat Wildlife Sanctuary stretch. WII has identified  and trained 26 Ganga Praharis from Bahraich distri ct to 
support aquatic biodiversity conservation along the Geruwa (Girwa) and Ghaghra rivers.  
Dredging/de-silting of rivers is not considered tec hno-economically feasible, as the benefits are 
generally marginal and effective only for a short d uration. De-silting measures, including dredging in  specific 
reaches of rivers for the removal of drainage conge stion, channel capacity improvement and navigation 
purposes, are formulated and implemented by the con cerned States/agencies, as required, based on prope r 
scientific model studies. For the comprehensive and  holistic management of sediments, the Department o f 
Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuve nation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, in extensive 
consultations with Central Ministries/Departments a nd State Governments/UTs, has prepared the “Nationa l 
Framework for Sediment Management ”.  The Framework emphasizes reducing silt generation rather than silt 
removal and promotes technological innovations and best practices. It also lays emphasis on sediment 
management through integrated river basin managemen t plans, giving due consideration to the environmen t 
and ecology. 
 *****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- ✝710 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 23/07/2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF FOREST RIGHTS ACT, 2006 
  
✝710. SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the large number of eligible tribal families across the country have not yet received 
the benefits of land leases under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006 and the other prevailing 
provisions and if so, the details thereof, State-wise;  
  
(b) whether coordination is being maintained by the Government with the States to provide 
land leases to eligible tribal families under individual and community forest rights in a time-
bound manner and for the early disposal of pending claims and if so, the details thereof;  
  
(c) the details of the claims received, land leases distribution approved, cases pending and 
claims rejected during the last three years, State-wise;  
  
(d) whether the Government is implementing any coordinated action plan to link eligible tribal 
families with irrigation, housing, agriculture, livelihood and other development schemes after 
they receive land leases; and  
  
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGA DAS UIKEY) 
  
(a) to (c): The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest 
Rights) Act, 2006 recognizes the different usufruct rights of the Forest Dwelling Tribal 
Communities and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers to forest resources, on which these 
communities were dependent for a variety of needs, including livelihood, habitation and other 
socio-cultural needs. Upon determination of eligibility under the provisions of the Act, eligible 
individuals are granted heritable forest rights. However, such rights are neither alienable nor 
transferable. The State Governments are responsible for implementation of various provisions 
of the Act. As per the latest information reported by the States and collated under MPR as on 
30.06.2026, a total of 25,42,359 Titles have been distributed comprising 24,18,197 Individual 
Forest Rights (IFR) Titles and 1,24,162 Community Forest Rights (CFR) Titles. A statement 
showing state wise details of titles distributed under FRA as on 30.06.2026 is at Annexure. 
  
  
  During the last three years i.e. from 30.06.2023 to 30.06.2026, a total of 8,46,958 
claims have been filed, a total of 2,30,318 Claims have been approved (Titles Distributed), 
11,671 claims have been rejected and a total of 6,04,969 claims are pending for decision. 

Further, the details of number of claims (individual and community) received, the number of 
claims approved (Title distributed), Claims rejected, Claims disposed off during the last three 
years, month- wise and State/UT-wise are available at this Ministry’s website- on FRA- 
MPR-  https://tribal.nic.in/FRA.aspx. 
  
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, being the Nodal Ministry for administering the 
legislative matters of FRA, exhorts all State Governments to abide by the provisions contained 
in FRA and ensure that all eligible claimants are provided the rights which are due to them.   
  
(d) & (e): As stipulated in Rule 16 of FRA, the State Government has to ensure through its 
departments that all government schemes, including those relating to land improvement, land 
productivity, basic amenities and other livelihood measures, are provided to such claimants 
and communities whose rights have been recognized and vested under the FRA. Further, the 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support to State Governments under the Dharti 
Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) for strengthening Gram Sabhas and 
Community Forest Resource Management Committees. Additionally, FRA patta holders are 
supported through convergence with schemes of the Department of Agriculture, Animal 
Husbandry and Fisheries, wherein beneficiary contribution has been limited to 10%, wherever 
required, to facilitate greater uptake. Further, eligible FRA title holders are covered under the 
PM-KISAN scheme implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.  
  
    The Ministry of Tribal Affairs continues to work with other Ministries / Departments for 
effective implementation and to ensure that benefits of these schemes reach forest right holders 
in full measure.

711.   Smt. Anita Nagarsingh Chouhan: 
          Dr. Nishikant Dubey: 
          Shri Arvind Dharmapuri: 
          Smt. Mala Rajya Laxmi Shah: 
          Shri Vijay Baghel: 
          Shri Jashubhai Bhilubhai Rathva: 
          Smt. Mahima Kumari Mewar: 
          Dr. Hemant Vishnu Savara: 
         Shri Bibhu Prasad Tarai:  
  
 Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
                                               
(a)  the features of the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) along with the 
classification of development works under the scheme; 
 (b) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of DAJGUA during 2026, if so, the outcome 
thereof: 
(c) the status of implementation of the interventions/projects under the Abhiyan, State-wise and district-
wise including the number of tribal-majority villages covered and beneficiaries covered so far; 
(d)  the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilized under the Abhiyan and other tribal development 
schemes in the country, State-wise;  
(e) whether the Government has identified delays or shortfalls in implementation, utilisation of funds or 
convergence of schemes under the Abhiyan in any State or Union Territory, if so, the details thereof and 
the steps taken to address the bottlenecks along with the timeline fixed for the same; and 
(f) the steps being taken to complete pending tribal development projects and improve delivery in 
education, health, housing, livelihood and connectivity sectors? 
  
  
  
                                                                ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY)                               
(a) The Government launched the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) for saturation 
of infrastructure and socio-economic development in identified tribal-majority villages through 
convergence of Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes implemented by multiple 
Ministries/Departments. The Abhiyan covers interventions relating to housing, rural connectivity, drinking 
water, health, education, hostels, Anganwadi Centres, mobile connectivity, electrification, renewable 
energy, LPG connections, tourism, livelihood, agriculture, fisheries, livestock, skill development, 
FRA/PESA awareness and capacity building, and other tribal welfare interventions. 
(b)  The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), being the nodal Ministry for the implementation of the Dharti 
Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), reviewed the progress of the scheme in a meeting 
attended by the concerned Line Ministries under DAJGUA and the State Tribal Welfare Departments. The 
review focused on the physical and financial progress of the interventions, implementation bottlenecks, 

fund flow, appraisal of proposals, convergence among the Line Ministries and the State/UT Governments, 
and measures required to expedite effective implementation of the scheme. 
  
The significant progress achieved under various interventions of Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram 
Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) includes the following: 
 
 13,02,811 houses have been sanctioned under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G). Out of 
sanctioned houses, 8,21,566 houses have been completed. 
 436 Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) have been operationalised to strengthen healthcare service delivery in 
tribal areas. 
 A total of 875 Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) have been sanctioned, out of which 681 AWCs have been 
made operational. 
 692 hostels have been sanctioned for tribal students, 4 hostels have been completed and the foundation

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 712 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
INCREASE IN AIRFARE  
712.      SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH   
             DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE                  
             PROF VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD               
             SMT SUPRIYA SULE                        
             SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE           
             SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL                   
             SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE  
           
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the significant increase in 
domestic and international airfares following the ongoing geopolitical tensions 
and conflict involving Iran and the United States which have led to higher 
aviation fuel costs and flight disruptions and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the increase in average air ticket prices on major routes 
connecting Maharashtra particularly Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur during the last 
six months; 
 
(c) whether the airlines have imposed fuel surcharge or revised fare structures 
due to rising Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices and longer flight routes and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to  monitor increases in airfare and 
protect passengers from excessive fare hikes; 
 
(e) whether any consultations have been held with airlines regarding fare 
rationalisation and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(f) the measures proposed to ensure affordable air connectivity for passengers 
travelling from Maharashtra? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 

(a) to (f): The ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia have significantly 
impacted ATF prices which has resulted in introduction of fuel surcharge in 
mid-March, 2026 by Indian carriers. 
 
The Fuel surcharge was introduced by the airlines in March, 2026 and was 
revised in the month of April 2026 based on flight distance. 
 
In order to ensure that airlines d o not charge airfares outside the range declared 
by them, Tariff Monitoring Unit (TMU) has been set up in Directorate General 
of Civil Aviation (DGCA) which monitors airfares on selected 78 routes (72 
domestic & 06 international) on random basis, including  three routes from 
Mumbai. 
 
The Government has taken several measures to support the aviation sector and 
help keep air travel affordable, which include, one -time budgetary support not 
exceeding Rs. 10,000 crores for Oil Markreting Companies (OMCs) to pro vide 
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) price stablisation support to the Scheduled Indian 
Airlines due to exceptional fuel price volatality arising from the West Asia 
crisis and for domestic operations, ATF prices were capped at a maximum 
increase of 25% over th e 1st March, 2026 base price, effective from 1st April 
2026 for the months of April and May, 2026. 
 
The issue of high VAT on ATF has been taken up with the States/ UTs by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation. As a result, 23 States/ UTs have reduced VAT on 
ATF since September 2021. More recently, in May, 2026, the State of 
Maharashtra has reduced the VAT on ATF from 18% to 7% for a period of 6 
months. 
 
Various factors influenced by combination of market forces like market 
competition, passenger demand, seat oc cupancy and seasonal variati ons, etc. 
also affect airfares. 
 
With the repeal of Air Corporation Act in March, 1994, airlines are free to 
establish airfare based on their operational & economic viability while adhering 
to Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937. 
 
The Government generally refrains from regulating airfares to maintain market 
competitiveness, however, it retains vigilant oversight role, intervening in 
exceptional circumstances by redistributing capacity across various sectors and 
imposing temporary fare caps, such as during the Covid Pandemic, festivals like 
Maha kumb or other extraordinary instances like Pahalgam incident &  the 
Indigo flight disruptions. 
 

Regular consultations are being carried out by DGCA with airlines from time to 
time, in order to sensitize to exercise moderation/ self - regulation while fixing 
the airfares and increasing capacity. 
******

entries.t: International Air Cargo Facilities in Punjab
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 715 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
INTERNATIONAL AIR CARGO FACILITIES IN PUNJAB  
715.    DR. AMAR  SINGH             
             
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the inadequate international air cargo 
facilities in Punjab despite the State's significant contribution to agricultural and 
industrial exports and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the present status of the proposals for establishing dedicated cargo terminals, 
cold-chain facilities, customs clearance and warehousing at Sri Guru Ram Dass 
Jee International Airport, Amritsar and Shaheed Bhagat Singh International 
Airport, Chandigarh; 
(c) whether representations have been received from trade and industry bodies 
seeking direct international cargo connectivity from Punjab and if so, the details 
thereof, including the action taken thereon; 
(d) the reasons for the non -availability of dedicated int ernational freighter 
services from Punjab; and 
(e) the steps taken to strengthen air cargo infrastructure, reduce export logistics 
costs and improve export competitiveness for farmers, Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and industries in Punjab? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e) The development of cargo facilities is a continuous process and 
depends on various factors such as airport development progress, increase in 
scheduled operations, handling capacity, growth in domestic cargo volumes and 
demand from airlines. The Government's approach is to provide suitable policy 
and congenial regulatory regime, for the encouragement of infrastructure 
development, simplification of procedures, te chnological upgradation, and 
deployment of skilled manpower, all aimed at efficient and cost -effective air 
cargo services delivery. 
 

The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has established an International Air 
Cargo Facility, including a Centre for Perishable Cargo (CPC), at Sri Guru Ram 
Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar. The facility is presently being operated 
by AAI Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Company Limited. Further, at 
Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh, which is oper ated by 
Chandigarh International Airport Limited, an Integrated Cargo Complex is 
available for cargo operations. 
 
The airlines initiate cargo operations based on their internal assessment of cargo 
potential, handling capabilities and overall commercial vi ability of operating 
from any airport. Further, the exporters, based on their commercial viability, 
requirements, utilize available air cargo facilities in accordance with various 
determining factors, including the destination country, airline operations, and 
the availability of direct or connecting services to the intended destinations. 
******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 716 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE  
716.    DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN                  
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the adequacy of airport infrastructure 
to meet the growing passenger and cargo traffic demand across the country and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of airports operating beyond their d esigned capacity and the 
measures proposed to address congestion and operational bottlenecks; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of infrastructure 
gaps relating to terminals, runways, cargo handling and air traffic management 
systems and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the investments proposed for modernisation and expansion of airport 
infrastructure in the next five years; and 
(e) whether any airport expansion, modernisation or greenfield airport projects 
are under consideration in Ka rnataka that would improve connectivity to 
districts such as Davanagere and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): Airport infrastructure, including passenger terminals , runways, 
aprons, cargo facilities and other airside infrastructure, is developed by the 
Airports Authority of India (AAI) and other airport operators based on traffic 
growth, operational requirements, airline demand, financial viability and 
techno-economic considerations. 
 
Expansion and modernisation projects undertaken at airports across the country 
have enhanced the total passenger -handling capacity to over 580 million 
passengers per annum (MPPA), while passenger traffic handled during 2025 -26 
was about 420 million. 
 

Passenger traffic varies across airports depending on factors such as seasonal 
demand, festivals, holidays and airline schedules, which may lead to temporary 
congestion during peak periods. Airport operators continuously monitor traffic 
and take necessary operational measures to ensure smooth passenger 
facilitation. 
 
In line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, airport development is being 
undertaken through Greenfield airports, revival of unserved and underserved 
airports under RCS -UDAN, e xpansion of existing airports, and promotion of 
private investment under the PPP mode. So far, 25 Greenfield airports have 
been accorded In -Principle Approval, of which 14 are operational, while 6 
proposals have been granted Site Clearance. Further, 95 aer odromes have been 
operationalised under RCS -UDAN (as on 10.07.2026). The modified UDAN 
Scheme envisages connectivity to 120 new destinations and serving 4 crore 
passengers over the next ten years. 
 
(e): Under the Greenfield Airports Policy, 2008, a develop er, including a State 
Government, is required to identify a suitable site, undertake a pre -feasibility 
study and submit a proposal to the Central Government for grant of Site 
Clearance followed by In-Principle Approval. No proposal for development of a 
Greenfield airport at Davanagere has been received from the Government of 
Karnataka. 
******

entries.t: Tap Water Connections in UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †719 
ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
  
TAP WATER CONNECTIONS IN UT OF DADRA AND NAGAR HAVELI AND 
DAMAN AND DIU 
  
†719. SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI: 
Will the Minister of Jal Shakti be pleased to state: 
(a) whether more than eighty per cent of rural households have been provided with tap water 
connections under the Har Ghar Jal component of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in the country 
as of July, 2026; 
(b) if so, the details thereof in respect of the Union Territory (UT) of Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
and Daman and Diu; 
(c) the details of rural households provided with tap water connections during the last two years 
till date, State-wise; and 
(d) the details of the funds allocated, released and utilised under the said Mission in respect of 
the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu during the last two years till date? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) & (b) Drinking water is a State subject. The power to plan, design, approve and implement 
drinking water supply schemes/projects lies with State/UT Government. Government of India, 
in partnership with States/UTs is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission, since August , 2019, to 
make provision of tap water supply of prescribed quality on a regular and long -term basis to 
every rural household. 
Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of Jal Jeevan Mission, 
towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the start of Jal Jeevan Mission 
in August 2019, only 3.23 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections. As on 20.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households in the country, more than 
15.89 crore (82.10%) households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. 
Dadra Nagar Haveli & Daman Diu had reported in 2022 that they had provided tap water 
connection to all rural households in the UT. (Source: JJM-IMIS). 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(c) The details of rural househo lds provided with tap water connections during the last two 
years till date, State-wise under the Jal Jeevan Mission in rural areas is in public domain and 
available on JJM dashboard at: https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx 
(d) No funds have b een released to the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 
during the last two years till date under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM). The details are available 
on JJM Dashboard (https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/jjmindia.aspx). 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
PLI SCHEME IN MADHYA PRADESH 
  
720. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of projects approved and the investment realised under Production Linked 
Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) in Madhya Pradesh along 
with the employment generated therefrom; 
(b) whether the Ministry has identified the Satna-Vindhya region as a potential agri-food 
processing cluster considering its production of tomato, onion and other horticultural 
crops and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether proposals for integrated processing, value-addition, cold-chain and food 
preservation infrastructure in the region are under consideration and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken to promote Farmer-Producer Organisations (FPOs), food 
processing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and export-oriented value 
chains in Madhya Pradesh under the vision of Viksit Bharat, 2047? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH)

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS

TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 23, 2026 
 
'CITIES AS GROWTH HUBS' INITIATIVE UNDER THE URBAN CHALLENGE 
FUND 
 
NO. 721 SHRI TEJASVI SURYA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether implementation of the "Cities as Growth Hubs" initiative under 
the Urban Challenge Fund has commenced and if so, the details thereof 
including its implementation framework, funding pattern and the 
categories of projects proposed to be supported; 
(b) the criteria for selection of cities and projects along with the details of 
proposals received, shortlisted and approved, State/UT -wise including 
those from Karnataka; 
(c) whether urban governance, municipal finance and planning reforms 
have been prescribed as preconditions for availing assistance under the 
Fund and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether measurable outcome indicators and targets relating to private 
investment mobilisation, infrastructure creation, municipal reforms and 
economic development have been prescribed under the initiative and if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a) to (d): The Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) scheme has been 
operationalized with the launch of Operational Guidelines for UCF on 15th 
April, 2026. UCF supports the development and strengthening of urban 
infrastructure through implementation of transformativ e and impactful 
projects under three verticals namely ‘Cities as Growth Hubs’, ‘Creative 
Redevelopment of Cities’ and ‘Water and Sanitation’.   
All Cities are eligible to participate under UCF. Chapter 7 of the operational 
guidelines includes details regarding the Project Appraisal and Challenge 
Framework including mandatory eligibility requirements, overall project 
flow/ implementation framework, and project evaluation process for 
…2/- 

-2- 
appraisal and selection of projects. The list of admissible projects under 
UCF are given under Chapter 5 of the operational guidelines. The scheme 
guidelines are in public domain and may be accessed at 
https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/04/7950afb9b2d5cb773ba3d
6c64bde9726.pdf 
Under UCF, Central Assistance is limited to 25 per cent of the cost of 
bankable projects, with the stipulation that at least 50 per cent of the 
project cost shall be financed through market -based sources, including 
municipal bonds, bank loans and Public- Private Partnerships (PPPs). The 
remaining project cost is to be met by the concerned State/UT/ULB. 
So far, 33 projects have been approved/ accorded in -principle approval 
including 3 projects from State of Karnataka.  The approved projects in 
Karnataka include sewerage infrastructure aimed at enhancing sewage 
treatment capacity and improving environmental outcomes, as well as 
major urban transport infrastructure such as flyovers and a section of the 
Peripheral Ring Road in Bengaluru to help decongest traffic and improve 
urban mobility.  The State-wise details are given in Annexure.  
Further, reforms implementation is an integral feature of the UCF. The 
reform provisions under the Scheme are contained in Chapter 8 of the 
Operational Guidelines. States/UTs are required to submit a reform 
roadmap and report progress to the Ministry. The reforms broadly cover 
Market & Financial Reforms, Governance & Digital Reforms, Operational & 
Capacity Reforms, Urban Planning & Spatial Reforms, Project -Specific 
Reforms (UCF -linked) to strengthen municipal governance, financial 
sustainability & service delivery which will in turn aid implementation of 
projects under UCF. 
The Guidelines also provide for monitoring of project outcomes through 
measurable indicators, including mobilisation of market -based finance, 
infrastructure creation and implementation of project-linked reforms.

EXPANSION OF NATURAL GAS INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
722. SMT. RACHNA BANERJEE: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the Government's target to increase the share of natural gas in India's energy 
mix; 
(b) the details of the progress made in expanding the National Gas Grid and City Gas Distribution 
(CGD) network during the last three years, year-wise and State/UT-wise; and 
(c) the challenges being faced in achieving universal access to piped natural gas (PNG) and 
compressed natural gas (CNG)? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): As per Energy Statistics 2026 released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, the share of natural gas in India's total primary 
energy supply was 7.12% (provisional) during Financial Year 2024–25. For increasing the share of 
natural gas in the energy basket, Government has taken various steps which inter-alia, include 
expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline, expansion of City Gas Distribution (CGD) network, setting 
up of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Terminals, allocation of domestic gas to Compressed Natural 
Gas (Transport)/ Piped Natural Gas (Domestic) CNG (T)/PNG(D) on priority, allowing marketing 
and pricing freedom with a ceiling price to gas produced from high pressure/high temperature areas, 
deep water & ultra-deep water and from coal seams, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable 
Transportation (SATAT) initiative to promote Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) etc. 
The National Gas Grid expansion is a continuous process. PNGRB authorizes entities to lay, build, 
operate and expand Natural Gas Pipelines (NGPL) across the country. The progress made in 
expansion of the National Gas Grid during the last three years is at Annexure-I. 
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural Gas 
(CNG) stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia 

include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, 
commercial and industrial units and CNG to transport sector is being carried out by the entities 
authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). The details of State/UT-wise 
CNG stations & DPNG connections progress for last three years is at Annexure-II. 
As informed by authorized CGD entities, challenges in achieving universal access to PNG and CNG, 
inter-alia, include: 
(i) High capital investment requirements for development of CGD infrastructure, particularly 
in sparsely populated and remote areas. 
(ii) Delay in obtaining statutory permissions/Right of Use (RoU)/Right of Way (RoW) and 
other approvals from various Central, State and local authorities for laying pipelines and 
establishing CNG stations. 
(iii) Land availability for installation of CNG stations, City Gate Stations (CGS) and other 
associated infrastructure. 
(iv) Availability and timely connectivity to the Natural Gas pipeline network, especially in 
areas where trunk pipeline infrastructure is under development. 
(v) Geographical and terrain-related constraints, including hilly, forest, coastal and difficult-
to-access areas, which increase project complexity and cost.

POLICY TO REDUCE OVER-DEPENDENCE ON COAL 
 
730. SHRI BIPLAB KUMAR DEB: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has formulated any policy to reduce over -
dependence on coal and promo te the integration of renewable energy sources 
and if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(b)  the outcome of such measures in terms of improving power supply 
reliability and sustainability during the last three years? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : India’s updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) outlines 
voluntary actions for transitioning towards a low -carbon pathway, including 
increasing the share of non -fossil-fuel-based energy and reducing the emissions 
intensity of GDP. The updated NDC target inter alia contains the target of 
achieving about 50% cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil 
fuel-based sources by 2030.The target of 50% of installed electric capacity from 
non-fossil fuel sources was achieved nearly five years ahead of schedule.  
 
Third version of India’s NDCs were submitted in March 2026 to the United 
Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) , to achieve 60% 
cumulative electric power installed capacity from non -fossil fuel-based energy 
resources by 2035.  
 
In line with these targets, Government of India has consistently diversified 
its electricity generation mix to strengthen the energy security. As on 30.06.2026, 
the country’s total installed generation capacity has reached to 5,48,858 M ega 
Watt (MW), comprising of 2,51,489 MW (45.82 % of total  installed capacity) of 
fossil-fuel sources i.e. Coal & Lignite, Gas, Diesel and 2,97,369 MW (54.18 % of 
total installed capacity) of non-fossil fuel sources i.e. Solar, Wind, Hydro, Nuclear 
and Biomass. The Government has taken several steps for promotion  of 
Renewable Generation and its integration. The  details are enclosed at     
Annexure-I.

share of Renewable Energy in meeting the country's electricity demand, along 
with a continuous reduction in the gap between energy requirement and energy 
supplied in the country. The details of all India energy requirement and supply 
status as well as percentage contribution from renewable energy sources, for last 
three years, are enclosed at Annexure-II.

2030. During Financial Year 2025-26 alone, India added around 55.3 GW of non -fossil 
generation capacity, including 44.6 GW of solar capacity and 6.1 GW of wind capacity.

environment friendly source of base load power. The lifecycle emissions of nuclear

& Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) projects have been issued. 
 
vii. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has been permitted up to 100 percent under the

TO BE ANSWERED ON 23 JULY, 2026 
Affordability and Supply of LPG 
 
732. MR PATHAN YUSUF: 
 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to take any further measures to reduce the retail price 
of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and to ensure affordable cooking fuel for economically 
weaker households, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of beneficiaries who have availed LPG subsidy under the Pradhan Mantri 
Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) during the last three years, year-wise; and 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to ensure uninterrupted supply of LPG across the 
country during recent international supply disruptions? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुर ेश गोपी) 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): Prices of LPG in the country are linked to its prices in the international 
market. Government continues to modulate the effective price to consumer for domestic 
LPG. 
Prior to the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East in February 2026, India used to import 
about 60 percent of its LPG consumption, out of which about 90 percent was transiting 
through the Strait of Hormuz. With the closure of Strait of Hormuz, supplies of imported 
LPG were severely constrained. The Government took a series of proactive measures to 
ensure stability in LPG supplies post the outbreak of the conflict. These include rapid 
increase in production of LPG from 34 to 54 TMT per day, prioritization of household usage 
of LPG, diversification of import sources, dynamic stock management, inter-regional 
allocation to address localized shortages, etc. Despite this unprecedented crisis, supply of 
LPG to all households in the country has been ensured without any disruption. During the 
peak of this crisis, more than 56 crore domestic LPG cylinders were delivered between 
March and June 2026, including more than 12 crore cylinders to Ujjwala families.  
As a result of the West Asia crisis, the average Saudi CP (the international benchmark for 
LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as the Saudi CP 
rose further to US$ 796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price (MDP) of a 
14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went upto Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder. However, the 
Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg cylinder. 
For Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) consumers, the effective price is Rs. 642 per 
cylinder in July 2026 after a targeted subsidy of Rs. 300 per cylinder. 
Government has paid a compensation of Rs. 22,000 crore to OMCs in FY 2022-23 and has 
approved another compensation of Rs. 30,000 crore in FY 2025-26 for under-recoveries on 
sale of domestic LPG.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a): Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched in May, 2016 with an objective to 
provide deposit free LPG connection to adult women from poor households across the 
country. As on 01.07.2026, there are approximately 10.58 crore PMUY connections across 
the country. All PMUY connections released under the scheme continue to remain active 
beneficiaries. State/UT-wise and year-wise details of PMUY connections released since 2020 
are at Annexure–A. 
 
(b): State/UT-wise details of number of PMUY Beneficiaries who have not taken any refill, 
number of PMUY Beneficiaries who have taken 1 to 4 refills and number of PMUY 
beneficiaries who have taken more than four refills during the FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26 are 
at Annexure – B. 
 
(c):  With the onset of the West Asia crisis, the average Saudi CP (the international 
benchmark for LPG pricing) rose upto US$ 780/MT in April and May 2026. In June 2026, as 
the Saudi CP rose further to US$ 796/MT (excluding premium), the Market Determined Price 
(MDP) of a 14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder went to Rs. 1,695 per 14.2 Kg cylinder.  
 

The Retail Selling Price of domestic LPG is being maintained at Rs. 942 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder, carrying an implicit subsidy (under-recovery) of more than Rs 700 per 14.2 Kg 
cylinder, in June 2026. Even for the month of July 2026, the implicit subsidy on each 14.2 Kg 
domestic LPG cylinder is more than Rs 500 per cylinder. For more than 10.5 crore PMUY 
consumers, the effective price is only Rs. 642 per cylinder (Delhi), after a targeted subsidy of 
Rs. 300 per cylinder, in addition to the implicit subsidy of more than Rs 500 per cylinder.  
Even after the reduction in number of refills eligible for targeted subsidy for PMUY 
households, all the consumers continue to avail implicit subsidies (under-recovery) of more 
than Rs. 500 per cylinder during July 2026. 
 
(d) Based on an assessment of FY 2025–26 refill consumption data, it has been observed that 
refill consumption patterns vary across PMUY beneficiary households, with a substantial 
proportion of beneficiaries availing up to four subsidised refills annually. The assessment 
further indicates that the targeted subsidy framework under PMUY has contributed to 
sustained adoption and regular usage of LPG as a clean cooking fuel. The per Consumer 
Consumption (PCC) among PMUY beneficiaries is 4.71 cylinders per year in FY 2025–26.  
 
In view of the refill average during FY 2025–26, provision of targeted subsidy support for up 
to four refills annually has been assessed as appropriate for continuing affordability support 
to PMUY beneficiary households, while enhancing targeting efficiency and ensuring prudent 
rationalisation of subsidy expenditure. The proposed rationalisation pertains only to the 
number of refills eligible for targeted subsidy and does not impose any restriction on the 
purchase of additional LPG refills at market prices which is also heavily subsidized at current 
RSP. 
 
(e): PMUY has had a significant positive impact on the lives of rural households, especially

methods that involve burning solid fuels like wood, dung and crop residues. The use of 
cleaner fuel lowers indoor air pollution, leading to improved respiratory health, particularly 
among women and children who are traditionally more exposed to household smoke.

URBAN WATER REQUIREMENTS IN TAMIL NADU 
 
736. THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a)   whether the Union Government is aware of the fact that rapid urbanisation in Theni, 
Periyakulam, Bodinayakanur and Cumbum in Theni Lok Sabha Constituency has increased 
water demand and if so, whether any assessment has been undert aken regarding the future 
urban water requirements in these towns and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Union Government is extending any technical and financial assistance to Urban 
Local Bodies for reduction of transmission losses and non-revenue water and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(c)   whether treated wastewater reuse projects are being encouraged in medium -sized towns 
of Tamil Nadu to reduce pressure on freshwater resources, if so, the details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) To enable every rural household in the country, including those in the Theni Lok Sabha 
Constituency, to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity of prescribed quality on 
regular and long-term basis, through tap water connection, since August 2019, Government of 
India in partnership with states, is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar Jal. 
At the start of the Mission, around 0.55 lakh (29.53%) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connections in Theni district of Tamil Nadu. So far, as reported by the State, around 
1.30 lakh rural households have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. Thus, as 
on 20.07.2026, all the 1.85 lakh rural households in the d istrict are reported to have tap water 
supply in their homes. 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has informed that Water is a State subject 
and it provides financial and technical support to the States through its schemes/ Missions such 
as Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) / AMRUT 2.0 for 
improvement/ augmentation of basic infrastructure in the sectors of water supply, sewerage 

Page 2 of 3 
 
and septage management, water body rejuvenation and parks and green spaces through 
approved projects. 
AMRUT 2.0 is implemented in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities, enabling the cities to 
become 'self-reliant' and 'water secure'. Providing universal coverage of sewerage and septage 
management in 500 AMRUT cities is one of the major focus are as of AMRUT 2.0. 
Rejuvenation of water bodies and development of green spaces and parks are other components 
of the mission. 
MoHUA has also informed that rapid urbanisation is one of the reasons affecting urban 
resources including water resources. Under AM RUT 2.0, cities have prepared City Water 
Balance Plans (CWBPs), which include as -is assessment of water supply systems which help 
cities/ ULBs to identify gaps. City Water Balance Plan help cities to identify scope for projects 
focusing on the objectives of Mission. Based on the projects identified in City Water Balance 
Plans, City Water Action Plan (CWAP) are devised. These CWAPs are aggregated in the form 
of State Water Action Plans (SWAP). Further, the State High Powered Steering Committee 
(SHPSC) headed by the Chief Secretary of the State, consider and recommend/ approve the 
SWAPs under AMRUT 2.0. State Level Technical Committee (SLTC) headed by the 
Secretary, Urban Development & Housing Department provides technical support to the 
SHPSC in approving, monitoring and supervising the scheme at the State level. 
Under AMRUT 2.0, States/ UTs are empowered to select, appraise, prioritise and implement 
the projects within the broad framework of Mission guidelines. The projects recommended by 
the SHPSC are approved by the Apex Committee under the Mission at the MoHUA level. The 
projects taken up by the State of Tamil Nadu in Theni, Periyakulam, Bodinayakanur and

be pleased to state:- 
(a) the extent to which domestic and international flight operations in the 
country have been curtailed due to shortage of aviation fuel resulting from the 
ongoing conflict in the Gulf region; 
 
(b) whether the Government proposes to resume all su spended flight operations 
in view of the fuel crisis being resolved and if so, the details thereof including 
the steps taken to ensure a stable supply of Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF); and 
 
(c) the Government's plan and the timeline for commencement of the l ong-
pending Mangaluru-Tirupati flight service in view of the demand from devotees 
and tourists? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): As informed by the Indian scheduled carriers, they have not cu rtailed 
flight operations due to shortage of aviation fuel. 
 
(c): With the repeal of Air Corporations Act in March 1994, the Indian domestic 
aviation has been deregulated. It is therefore up to the airlines to provide air 
services to specific places depen ding upon the traffic demand and commercial 
viability subject to compliance with the extant guidelines in this regard. Airlines 
plan their domestic flight schedule on a specific route/city based on market 
demand, commercial feasibility and their company policy.

entries.head:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 744 
ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
 
FUNCTIONAL HOUSEHOLD TAP CONNECTIONS UNDER JJM IN BARMER 
DISTRICT 
 
744. SHRI UMMEDA RAM BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of Functional Household Tap Connections reported under the Jal Jeevan 
Mission (JJM) in Barmer district along with the number of such connections currently 
delivering water at the prescribed norm of fifty-five litres per capita per day on a regular basis 
and the details of connections found non -functional or delivering no water during any 
assessment conducted in the district; 
(b) the total number of tap connections reported and the number of functionally verified 
connections in Rajasthan keeping in view that Rajasthan is one of the States where JJM targets 
remain incomplete as of 2026 and the details of villages certified as Har Ghar Jal despite such 
connections not delivering regular water supply; and  
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce mandatory independent functionality 
verification before certifying any village as Har Ghar Jal in view of the Government's 
Functionality Assessment, 2024 which found that only seventy-six per cent of households with 
tap connections nationally receive water meeting basic standards, if so, the details thereof and 
if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) to (c) To enable every rural household in the country, including those in Barmer district of 
Rajasthan, to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity of prescribed quality on regular 
and long-term basis, through tap water connections, since August 2019, Government of India 
in partnership with States/UTs, is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar Jal. 
At the start of the Mission, around 11.74 lakh (10.91%) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connections in Rajasthan. So far, as reported by the State, around 51.89 la kh rural 
households have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, 

Page 2 of 2 
 
out of 107.65 lakh rural households in the State, around 63.63 lakh (59.10%) households are 
reported to have tap water supply in their homes. As on date, o ut of 42,327 villages in State, 
6,147 are certified as Har Ghar Jal.  
Similarly, at the start of the Mission, around 0.06 lakh (2.28%) rural households were reported 
to have tap water connections in Barmer district of Rajasthan. So far, as reported by the State, 
around 0.52 lakh rural households have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. 
Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 2.73 lakh rural households in the district, more than 0.58 lakh 
(21.37%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. 
The Operational Guidelines of JJM 2.0 envisages detailed verification and certification process 
for declaring a village as Har Ghar Jal. A village is considered for certification only after 
completion of all water supply schemes covering all households and public institutions. Before 
certification, the scheme is required to undergo a mandatory trial run of at least 15 days to 
ensure reliable and sustained water supply, followed by formal commissioning and handover 
to the Gram Panchayat through a Jal Arpan ceremony. Thereafter, the Gram Panchayat 
convenes a Gram Sabha in the presence of a representative of the District Water & Sanitation 
Mission (DWSM) to pass a resolution certifying that all households, public institutions and 
eligible habitations have been provided with functional tap water connections and access to 
safe drinking water as per the prescribed norms. The resolution, along with a brief video 
recording of the Gram Sabha proceedings, is uploaded on the JJM Dashboard and only 
thereafter is the village marked as Har Ghar Jal Certified in the JJM-IMIS.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 23rd July, 2026 
AVAILABILITY OF E-20 PETROL FOR NON-COMPATIBLE VEHICLES  
 
745. SHRI SHAHU SHAHAJI CHHATRAPATI: 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has made the sale of twenty per cent ethanol-blended petrol (E20) 
mandatory for all public and private fuel retailers across the country, thereby effectively 
phasing out E-10 and unblended petrol, if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether private oil marketing companies or specific retail outlets are permitted any 
exemption to sell lower ethanol-blended petrol to consumers whose vehicles are not E-20 
compliant, if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether the Government has taken cognizance of reports regarding accelerated engine wear, 
reduced fuel efficiency and subsequent motor insurance claim disputes relating to older 
vehicles using E-20 fuel, if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)  the steps being taken by the Government to ensure that fuel compatibility options remain 
accessible for the millions of non-compatible two-wheelers and passenger vehicles currently 
on the road? 
 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) & (b) :  In accordance with the Government's policy for implementation of the Ethanol 
Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, Oil Marketing Companies have been directed to supply Ethanol 
Blended Motor Spirit containing up to 20% ethanol, conforming to the relevant Bureau of Indian 
Standards (BIS) specifications, across all States and Union Territories.  
Further, with effect from 1 April 2026, Ethanol Blended Motor Spirit with a minimum Research 
Octane Number (RON) of 95 has been notified under the relevant statutory provisions.  
(c):     The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, 
scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, 
Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Society of 
Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) and other technical 
institutions. 

Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, with countries such as Brazil 
operating higher ethanol blends for decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme 
commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending remained 
around 1.53% in 2013-14, it has since been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after 
creating the necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
 
The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with 
automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs). 
The Government has not received any widespread or substantiated complaints from vehicle 
manufacturers, automobile associations or consumer organisations regarding the use of E20 petrol 
with respect to fuel efficiency, engine performance, maintenance costs and the overall driving 
experience. The Government has, however, taken note of certain concerns raised in media and social 
media, which have been scientifically examined. 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 
validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 
The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-
a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and 
over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer 
service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 
fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing 
further confidence in its safety and reliability.

The details of food processing units Sanctioned, Operational, Project Cost and Subsidy 
approved along with employment generated in Warangal district under the various schemes of 
the Ministry during the last three years, scheme-wise are at Annexure.   
To promote food processing industries and value addition to agricultural produce in Warangal 
district, the PMFME Scheme provides financial, technical and business support through 35% 
credit-linked capital subsidy, Seed Capital support to SHG members, Capacity Building, 
Common Infrastructure, and Branding & Marketing assistance. 
PMKSY is a Central Sector umbrella scheme aimed at creating modern food processing and 
preservation infrastructure, minimizing post-harvest losses, adding value to agricultural 
produce and enhancing farmers' income. PMKSY is demand driven in nature and applications 
are invited through Expression of Interest (EoI) from all over India including Warangal district. 
The funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released State-wise under any of the component 
schemes of PMKSY. The proposals received are scrutinized for their eligibility and evaluated 
based on the criteria fixed as per the extant scheme guidelines. Merit based approvals are given 
to the eligible proposals based on availability of funds 
PLISFPI is, inter alia, intended to support creation of global food manufacturing champions 
and support Indian brands of food products in international market. The Scheme is operational 
for a period from 2021-22 to 2026-27 with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crores. However, no projects 
have been sanctioned under PLISFPI, in Warangal district of Telangana. 

  
Ministry promotes the food processing sector and value addition to agricultural produce 
through creation of modern processing infrastructure and efficient supply chain management 
from farm gate to retail outlet. The interventions support development of storage, 
transportation, processing, value addition and other post-harvest infrastructure, thereby 
reducing post-harvest losses and wastage of agricultural produce, enhancing processing levels 
and productivity, improving value realisation for farmers, and increasing the competitiveness 
and export potential of processed food products.

749. THIRU ARUN NEHRU: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a)   whether the Government is aware of the severe and prolonged shortage of drinking water 
in villages such as V. Kalathur in Veppanthattai Taluk and in Perambalur Municipality (21 
wards) falling under Perambalur Lok Sabha Constituency leading to  public protests and road 
blockades and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the present status of drinking water supply in the said areas; 
(c)   the present status and expected timeline for completion of the Combined Water Supply 
Scheme (CWSS) from the Kollidam River for which Rupees 366.50 crore has been allocated; 
and 
(d) the steps taken to provide immediate relief through water tankers and other alternative 
arrangements until the scheme becomes fully operational? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
 
(a) to (d) To enable every rural household in the country, including those in Perambalur Lok 
Sabha Constituency, to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity of prescribed quality 
on regular and long-term basis, through tap water connection, since August 2019, Government 
of India in partnership with States, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar 
Jal. 
At the start of the Mission, around 0.06 lakh (2.28%) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connections in Perambalur district of Tamil Nadu. So far, as reported by the State, 
around 0.52 lakh rural households have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. 
Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 2.73 lakh rural households in the district, more than 0.58 l akh 
(21.37%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. Moreover, as 
reported by the State, V. Kalathur Gram Panchayat in Veppanthattai block of Perambalur 

Page 2 of 2 
 
district have already achieved Har Ghar Jal status i.e. 100% households have tap water supply 
in their homes. 
As drinking water being a state subject, under JJM, responsibilities for planning, approval, 
implementation, operation and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes lie with State/ 
UT governments. The details of villages being provided drinking water through water tankers 
are maintained at state government level. 
As informed by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), it provides financial and 
technical support to the States through its schemes/ Missions such as Atal  Mission for 
Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 2.0 (AMRUT 2.0) for improvement/ augmentation 
of basic infrastructure in the sectors of water supply, sewerage and septage management, 
water body rejuvenation and parks and green spaces through approved projects.  
AMRUT 2.0 is launched in the year 2021 in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ cities, enabling 
the cities to become 'self-reliant' and 'water secure'. Providing universal coverage of sewerage 
and septage management in 500 AMRUT cities is one of the maj or focus areas of AMRUT 
2.0. Rejuvenation of water bodies and development of green spaces and parks are other 
components of the mission. Under the Mission, States/ Union Territories (UTs) are 
empowered to select, appraise, prioritize and implement projects. 
Under AMRUT 2.0, the State of Tamil Nadu has taken up 3 projects worth ₹374.22 crore 
(including operation and Maintenance cost) in Perambalur Municipality, which includes 1 
water supply project worth ₹373.93 crore, 1 water body rejuvenation project worth  ₹0.11 
crore and 1 park project worth ₹0.18 crore. 
As per the progress reported by the State on AMRUT 2.0 portal, as on 09.07.2026, the water 
supply project titled ‘Combined Water Supply Scheme to Perambalur Municipality and State 
Industries Promotion Corp oration of Tamil Nadu (SIPCOT) Industrial Complex located at 
Erayur and Padalur in Perambalur District with River Kollidam as source’ is 92% physically 
completed.

CONSTRUCTION OF NATIONAL HIGHWAY PROJECTS 
  
752.    SHRI RAHUL KASWAN:  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any comprehensive evaluation 
regarding progress, cost, timelines and regional balance of the Bharatmala 
Pariyojana, Economic Corridors and other National Highway projects during the 
last three years and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the details of National Highway projects sanctioned, under construction and 
completed, State-wise including Rajasthan;  
(c) whether th e Government has reviewed the projects delayed due to land 
acquisition, forest clearances, utility shifting and other reasons and if so, the 
major reasons therefor and the solutions proposed therein; and  
(d) the new monitoring and project management syste ms developed by the 
Government to ensure the timely completion of National Highway projects? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) and (b) Bharatmala Pariyojana  Phase-I was approved by the Government   in 
2017, covering a length of 34,800 km across the Country at an estimated outlay 
of Rs. 5,35,000 Crore. Under the programme, projects covering a total length of 
26,425 km had been awarded. Out of this, 22,709 km ha ve already been 
constructed as of May 2026. State -wise details of the projects under 
Bharatmala Pariyojana are enclosed at Annexure-I. 
  
A study conducted by the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), 
Bangalore, to evaluate the impact of Bharatmala Pariyoja na indicates positive 
effects across multiple sectors. Economically, household income and 

expenditure have increased. Logistics efficiency has improved with reduced 
costs. Businesses have benefited from better access to markets and factories. 
Socially, tra vel time to schools and healthcare facilities has decreased, 
enhancing accessibility. Overall, the study suggests that Bharatmala 
Pariyojana has significantly contributed to socio-economic growth.  
  
The details of National Highway projects/length sanction ed, under 
construction and completed, State -wise including Rajasthan during the last 
three years are enclosed at Annexure-II, Annexure-III and Annexure-IV 
respectively. 
  
(c) The primary reasons for delay in National Highway (NH) projects are 
issues/bottlenecks relating to land acquisition, delay in getting statutory 
clearances, utility shifting, encroachment removal, law & order, non-availability 
of construction material/minerals, poor performance of 
Contractor/Concessionaire, and Force Majeur e events like the Covid -19 
pandemic etc. 
  
To expedite project execution, various initiatives have been undertaken, 
including streamlining the land acquisition process through the Bhoomi Rashi 
Portal, revamping the Parivesh Portal through Ministry of Envir onment, Forests 
& Climate Change (MoEFCC) to expedite forest and environmental clearances, 
enabling online approval of General Arrangement Drawings (GAD) for Road Over 
Bridges (ROBs) and Road Under Bridges (RUBs) from the Railways, and 
conducting review me etings at various levels with all stakeholders, including 
State Governments. The National Highway projects are regularly reviewed and 
monitored at various levels including through the Project Monitoring Group and 
"PRAGATI". 
  
(d)    Further, monitoring of NH projects is being done through Data Lake 3.0, a 
centralized GIS -based platform covering pre -construction, construction, and 
operation & maintenance stages. Data Lake 3.0 is scheduled to be fully 
operational by April 2027. 
 
Further, Artificial Intelligen ce/Machine Learning (AI/ML) -enabled drone 
monitoring is being used to validate physical progress through geo -tagged 
imagery and GIS-based dashboards integrated with the Data Lake.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 753 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
OUTCOME ASSESSMENT OF SCADA-IOT BASED IRRIGATION SYSTEMS 
753. Shri DUSHYANT SINGH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has initiated any outcom e-based evaluation framework for SCADA-IoT based 
irrigation systems under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and the Modernisation of 
Command Area Development and Water Management (MCAD WM) Scheme to assess improvements in 
water use efficiency, energy savings, irrigation reliability and crop productivity, particularly across the thirty-
two sanctioned clusters and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any baseline performance indicators hav e been prescribed for States to measure water savin gs, 
reduction in transmission losses and improvement in command area coverage and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps being taken to develop replicable nat ional models and best practice benchmarks across di fferent 
agro-climatic zones as envisaged by the Government for scaling technology-enabled irrigation 
modernisation; and 
(d) whether the findings from the pilot clusters in cluding the Bisalpur Right Main Canal cluster in Ra jasthan 
are proposed to be used for a broader national irrigation modernisation roadmap and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a)  Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was  launched during the year 2015-16, with an aim 
to enhance physical access of water on farm and expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve on-
farm water use efficiency, introduce sustainable water conservation practices, etc.  Technological innovations 
such as underground pipelines, micro-irrigation, SC ADA based monitoring etc. are promoted under Pradha n 
Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana- Accelerated Irrigat ion Benefits Programme (PMKSY-AIBP). States are 
encouraged to adopt such interventions for enhanced  water use efficiency. The list of some of the impo rtant 
projects under PMKSY-AIBP with SCADA as a component is at Annexure - I. 
Further, the Cabinet approved the Modernization of Command Area Development and Water 
Management (M-CADWM) as a sub-scheme of PMKSY on 09 .04.2025 for the period 2025-2026 to be 
implemented on pilot projects basis. The Scheme env isages monitoring of water use efficiency, water 
accounting and other performance parameters using S CADA, Internet of Things (IoT) and satellite-based 
technologies across the 38 sanctioned pilot cluster s. Total 38 nos. of such projects spreading over in  28 
States/UTs have been sanctioned ( Annexure-II ). 

2 
 
 
Water being State subject, it is for the State Gove rnment concerned to plan, implement and manage 
the irrigation projects, and to prepare action plan  to make irrigation system more extensive in the St ate. The 
role of Government of India is limited to providing  technical support, and partial ﬁnancial assistance  for 
identiﬁed projects under the ongoing schemes. 
(b)  The Modernization of Command Area Development and Water Management (M-CADWM) scheme 
provides for baseline indicators which include, cro pping intensity, water use efficiency, water produc tivity, 
farmers' participation, adoption of micro-irrigatio n and energy efficiency etc. During the Operation a nd 
Management phase, water use efficiency, water accou nting and other performance parameters are monitore d 
through SCADA, IoT and satellite-based systems.  
(c)  The M-CADWM Scheme envisages implementation of pil ot projects across different agro-climatic zones 
in the country incorporating institutional, technic al and management reforms and strategies in the com mand 
area development  and water management. Based on th e learnings in design and structuring of these 
projects, National Programme for Modernisation of C ommand Area Development and Water Management 
will be designed. In this regard, total 38 nos. of such projects in 28 States/UTs has been sanctioned for 
implementation (Annexure-II).  
(d)  Yes, based on the learnings in design and structuring of the 38 pilot clusters, including the Bisalpur Right 
Main Canal cluster in Rajasthan under M-CADWM schem e, the National Programme for Modernisation of 
Command Area Development and Water Management will be designed.
