entries.t: Usage of Sustainable Fuel in Aircrafts
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 799 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
USAGE OF SUSTAINABLE FUEL IN AIRCRAFTS  
799.    SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA           
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is considering the use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel 
(SAF) in aircraft and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the differences between the existing aviation fuel and Sustainable Aviation 
Fuel (SAF), including th e cost of production, environmental impact and 
operational challenges in aircraft operations; 
 
(c) the present availability of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF); and 
 
(d) whether crude oil would be required to be imported for SAF production and 
if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): As per the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), 
Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a drop -in aviation fuel produced from 
sustainable feedstocks such as used cooking oil, agricultural residues, municipal 
solid waste and other renewable or non -fossil sources and does not require 
crude oil as the primary feedstock, whereas Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) is a 
conventional aviation fuel derived from petroleum (crude oil).  
 
Being a drop -in fuel, SAF can be blended with conventional ATF and used in 
the existing aircraft engines and fuel systems without requiring any 
modification. Further, SAF has the potential to significantly reduce lifecycl e 
greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional ATF, thereby contributing 
to the decarbonisation of the aviation sector. However, the current production 
cost of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is higher than that of conventional 
Aviation Turbine Fuel ( ATF) due to developing technologies, limited 
production capacity and limited availability of sustainable feedstocks. 

 
The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% 
by 2028, and 5% by 2030 for SAF in conventional Aviation Turbin e Fuel for 
international operations. Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively 
engaged in achieving the stated blending targets. 
 
******

before completion of their 3 -year VGF support tenure and are non -operational. 6 
airports in Uttar Pradesh have become non -operational due to discontinuation of 
these routes.  
The above discontinued routes may be considered under the next phase of UDAN, 
with State Governments encouraged to identify and prioritize them for award based 
on regional connectivity needs, development objectives, and demand potential. 
There are 14 cases in which  penalties were imposed by forfeiture of Bank 
Guarantees against short performance during 2024-25 and 2025-26.  

 
(d) The underlying premise of UDAN scheme is to establish connectivity to 
unserved and underserved airports and regions. The scheme has facilita ted the 
development of airports, many of which have evolved to provide alternate flight 
and route options, thereby not losing out on connectivity.  
 
(e)To ensure continuity of services under the UDAN Scheme, State Governments 
have been entrusted with identi fying and prioritising high -potential aerodromes, 
while airlines are required to submit business plans before route awards. The 
Implementing Agency also publishes a list of ready or likely -to-be-ready 
aerodromes to facilitate timely operationalisation. Add itionally, discontinued 
eligible routes are re -bid in subsequent rounds and the Scheme permits route 
novation after award, allowing operational rights to be transferred to another 
eligible airline to maintain uninterrupted regional connectivity. 
The next p hase of the UDAN scheme strengthens the sustainability of routes 
through longer-duration VGF support with a tapered mechanism to allow sufficient 
time for route maturation. Airport sustainability concerns are being addressed by 
provision of dedicated O&M support for aerodromes.

KRISHI UDAN SCHEME FOR TAMIL NADU  
803.    SHRI MANI A                             
  
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government proposes to expand the benefits of the Krishi 
UDAN Scheme to farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations in Dharmapuri 
district of Tamil Nadu to facilitate the timely and cost -effective air 
transportation of mangoes, vegetables, flowers and other perishable horticultural 
produce to domestic and international markets and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the feasibility of establishing 
collection centres, pack houses, cold -chain in frastructure and refrigerated 
logistics linking Dharmapuri with the nearest airports under the Krishi UDAN 
Scheme and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any proposal has been received for improving air cargo connectivity 
for agricultural produce from Dharmapuri and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps proposed to be taken to reduce post -harvest losses, improve 
farmers' incomes and enhance export opportunities for horticultural produce 
from Dharmapuri under the Krishi UDAN Scheme? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) The Krishi Udan Scheme aims to ensure seamless, cost -effective, time -
bound, air transportation and associated logistics for all Agri -produce 
originating especially from the Northeast, hilly and tribal regions of the country, 
so that it improves their value realisation. All perishable commodities such as 
horticulture, fishery, livestock and processed products are covere d under the 
Krishi Udan Scheme. 
 
(b) The development of cargo facilities is a continuous process and depends on 
various factors such as airport development progress, increase in scheduled 
operations, handling capacity, growth in domestic cargo volumes and demand 

from airlines. The Government's approach is to provide suitable policy and 
congenial regulatory regime, for the encouragement of infrastructure 
development, simplification of procedures, technological upgradation, and 
deployment of skilled manpower, all aimed at efficient and cost -effective air 
cargo services delivery. 
 
(c) The airlines initiate cargo operations based on their internal assessment of 
cargo potential, handling capabilities and overall commercial viability of 
operating from any airport. Consequently, the decision to operate on any route 
rests with the airlines. 
 
(d) Under the Krishi Udan Scheme, in order to facilitate and incentivise 
movement of agri -produce by air transportation, reduce post -harvet losses, 
improve farmers' incomes and enhance export opportunities, waiver of landing 
and parking cha rges is provided for Indian freighters and P2C (Passenger -to-
Cargo) Aircraft by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and the Ministry of 
Defence at selected airports. In addition, Route Navigation Facility Charges 
(RNFC) and Terminal Navigational Landing Charges (TNLC) are waived at 
such selected AAI airports. Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export 
Development Authority (APEDA), also organizes training and capacity building 
programs in collaboration with concerned Ministries for its stakeholders t o 
sensitize its members regarding Government Schemes including Krishi Udan.

entries.head:
1 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI

LOK SABHA

STATUS OF JAL SHAKTI ABHIYAN IN TAMIL NADU 
806.  Shri THARANIVENTHAN M S: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA) including the number of districts and villages covered in 
Tamil Nadu since its launch; 
(b) the major outcomes and improvements achieved in  water conservation, groundwater recharge and 
watershed management under the said Abhiyan in Tamil Nadu including Arani Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(c) whether the Government has identified any chall enges or bottlenecks faced by States in effective 
implementation of the said abhiyan and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken to ensure community parti cipation, transparency and sustainable water resour ces 
management under the said Abhiyan? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) & (b)  Water is a State subject and the Central Governmen t supplements the efforts of the States through 
technical and financial support. Water conservation is one of the foremost priorities of the Government.  
The Ministry of Jal Shakti launched the Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA) in 2019 as a time-bound, mission-
mode water conservation campaign in 256 water stres sed districts of the country. The Hon'ble PM of Ind ia 
launched the campaign in 2021 as Jal Shakti Abhiyan : Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) with the message, "Catc h 
the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls." Since then, JSA: CTR evolved into a national movement, reinforcing 
India's collective commitment to water security thr ough localised action and institutional convergence . The 
JSA: CTR campaign was implemented nationwide in all  the districts (rural as well as urban) of the coun try 
including the state of Tamil Nadu and each edition had included a targeted focus since 2023 to maximiz e 
impact.  
To further deepen public involvement, "Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari" (JSJB) initiative was launched in 
Surat, Gujarat on 6th September 2024. In June 2025,  JSJB 2.0 was launched. The implementation cycle fo r 
JSJB 2.0 commenced on 1 June 2025 and concluded on 31 May 2026. Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the 
Rain (JSJB: CTR) – 2026 was launched on 1st June 20 26 enhancing the scope of the Jal Sanchay Jan 
Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative and simultaneously inte grating it with the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the R ain 
(JSA: CTR) campaign. 

2 
 
Under the Jal Shakti Abhiyan, 4,47,997 Water Conser vation & Rainwater Harvesting structures, 
44,494 Renovation of traditional water bodies, 5,67 ,550 Reuse and Recharge structures, 3,46,537 Waters hed 
Development structures are reported by the State Go vernment of Tamil Nadu which inter alia includes 17 ,962 
Water Conservation & Rainwater Harvesting structure s, 3,518 Renovation of traditional water bodies, 24 ,490 
Reuse and Recharge structures, 12,324 Watershed Dev elopment structures in Arani Lok Sabha Constituency . 
Also, the State Government of Tamil Nadu reported t hat all the districts and 12,480 Panchayats are cov ered 
under Jal Shakti Abhiyan since inception. 
(c)  ‘Water’ being a State subject, the aspects related t o water resources including its conservation are studied, 
planned, funded and executed by the State Governmen ts themselves as per their own resources and priori ties. 
The State Government of Tamil Nadu informed that it  has successfully implemented Jal Shakti Abhiyan 
campaign in the state through inter-departmental coordination with various stakeholder departments like water 
resources, rural development, agriculture and urban bodies. 
(d)  ‘Water’ being a State subject, the responsibility fo r the conservation and management of water resource s, 
including public awareness generation, primarily rests with the State Governments and local bodies. However, 
the Government of India undertook several initiativ es including Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JS A: 
CTR) across the country to sensitize the public abo ut the importance of water conservation and to prom ote 
behavioral changes in water usage patterns. Awarene ss generation is one of the five focused interventi ons of 
JSA: CTR campaign which aimed at spreading public a wareness about water-related challenges and the 
importance of conservation, with an emphasis on tur ning water conservation into a people’s movement (J an 
Andolan). 
As part of JSA: CTR, States and Union Territories w ere requested to establish Jal Shakti Kendras 
(JSKs) in all districts. These Kendras function as resource and knowledge centers, providing informati on on 
water-related issues, showcasing best practices, offering technical support, and serving as local hubs  for water 
conservation strategies. 712 Jal Shakti Kendras have been established across the country including 38 JSKs in 
Tamil Nadu. 
The JSJB ini

808. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
   
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details regarding cyberattacks, malware, unauthorised access 
and other cybersecurity  incidents involving vehicles and vehicle 
software systems reported across the country; 
(b) the details of the existing regulatory framework governing 
cybersecurity and software  update management in technologically 
advanced vehicles, including the categories of vehicles  covered and 
the standards prescribed; 
(c) wh ether any gaps have been identified in the existing framework 
for securing vehicle  software systems, including battery management 
systems against cyber threats and if so, the  steps taken or proposed 
to be taken to address the same; 
(d) the mechanism for te sting, certification, monitoring and 
enforcement of vehicle  cybersecurity and software update systems 
and the agencies responsible for the same; and 
(e) the steps taken or proposed to align India's vehicle cybersecurity 
standards with applicable  international regulations and to strengthen 

cybersecurity and software update management in  connected and 
advanced technology vehicles? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has 
received reports of safety concern involving electric three-wheelers (e-
rickshaws). It has been reported that it is possible for unauthorized 
individuals to abruptly power off moving e -rickshaws by using a 
publicly available BMS mobile application. 
CERT-In has identified the mobile apps which can be used to abruptly 
power-off batteries of e-rickshaws and reported to MeitY to remove the 
apps from application play stores. 
(b) The Government in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
vide G.S.R. 503(E) dated 17th June, 2026 has published draft rules for 
cyber security in respect of vehicles of category L, M and N as per AIS- 
189 and AIS- 190 inviting comments and objections. 
(c) and (e) With a view to harmonising the national standards with th e 
internationally accepted regulatory framework, the provisions of UN 
Regulation No. 155  on Cybersecurity and Cybersecurity Management 
Systems (CSMS) and UN Regulation No. 156  on Software Update and 
Software Update Management Systems (SUMS) were transposed and 
AIS-189, titled Approval of Vehicles with regard to Cybersecurity and 
Cybersecurity Management System (CSMS), and AIS-190, titled 
Approval of Vehicles with regard to Soft ware Update and Software 
Update Management System (SUMS), were formulated to establish the 
technical and procedural requirements for the approval of motor 

vehicles concerning cybersecurity and over -the-air (OTA) software 
updates. 
(d) Rule 126 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR), 1989 
mandates that every manufacturer or importer of a motor vehicle, 
including electric vehicles, shall submit the prototype to a testing 
agency notified under Rule 126. The testing agency issues a Type 
Approval Certifi cate certifying compliance with the provisions of the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the CMVR, 1989.

 GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DELAYS IN IMPLEMENTATION OF JAL JEEVAN MISSION 
810. SHRI SAPTAGIRI SANKAR ULAKA:           
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the delays in implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission 
(Har Ghar Jal) and if so, the details thereof, State -wise including the reasons for time and cost 
overruns;  
(b) whether the Government has received reports that execution of new water supply projects has led 
to damage to existing roads, drainage systems, pipelines and other public infrastructure without 
timely restoration and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the number of incomplete, delayed or non -functional water supply projects under the Mission, 
State-wise including Odisha;  
(d) whether any performance audit or third-party quality assessment has been conducted to examine 
project execution, restoration of public assets and accountability of implementing agencies and if so, 
the details thereof; and  
(e) the measures taken to ensure timely completion of projects, restoration of damaged infrastructure, 
quality control and uninterrupted safe drinking water supply to rural households? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) to (c) Drinking Water is a ‘State’ subject, and hence, under JJM, the responsibility of planning, 
approval, implementation, operation & maintenance of drinking water supply schemes lies with 
State/UT Governments. The Gov ernment of India supports the States by providing technical and 
financial assistance.  
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/ UTs, is implementing Jal Jeevan 
Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal to make provision of tap water connection to every rural household of 
the country. The Union Cabinet has approved extension of the JJM up to December 2028, with an 
enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation framework focusing on structural reforms in the 
rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
States/ UTs have informed that lack of dependable drinking water sources in water stressed, 
drought   prone and desert areas, presence of geogenic contaminants in ground water, uneven 
geographical terrain, scattered rural habitations, delay in release of the matching State share in some 
States, lack of technical capacity with implementing agencies, Gram Panchayats and local 
communities to plan, manage, operate & maintain the water supply schemes, delay in obtaining 

Page 2 of 2 
 
statutory/ other clearances, etc. are some of the challenges faced in the implementation of the mission. 
However, the operational guidelines for the implementation of the JJM, stipulates that time and cost 
overrun shall not be supported under JJM. 
Since water is a state subject, the responsibility of implementation, inter -alia including repairing or 
restoration of roads that get affected while laying water supply pipelines of rural water supply 
schemes taken up under JJM, lies with State/ UT Governm ents and the funds available under JJM 
may be utilized for the same. The public grievances pertaining to JJM received in Department, inter 
alia, including restoration of roads, are forwarded to the respective States for their expeditious 
redressal. Further, to avoid any hardships to the villagers, States/ UTs have been advised to take up 
rural water schemes in a way with minimum damages to infrastructure such as roads/ highways and 
to restore the roads/ highways immediately in case of damages done while lay ing of pipelines for 
water supply systems.  
At the start of JJM, only 3.23 crore (16.7%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections. So far, as reported by States/ UTs, more than 12.66 crore additional rural households 
have been provided with tap water connections under JJM. Thus, as on 15.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore 
rural households in the country, more than 15.89 crore (82.09%) households are reported to have tap 
water supply in their homes and works for the remaining 3.47 crore households are at various stages 
of implementation in respective States. As numerous projects are implemented concurrently at 
various levels across the States for achieving the envisaged objectives, project -wise details of 
individual projects/ schemes for rural water supply projects are maintained at the State Government 
level. The State -wise details of tap connections including those in Odisha is in public domain and 
may be accessed at below link: https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMState.aspx

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has finalised the guidelines for the recently 
approved Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely the "Urban Challenge 
Fund" and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether private sector entities would have control over the projects 
under the Urban Challenge Fund and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Urban Challenge Fund is proposed to replace the existing 
Central schemes for urban infrastructure development and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Union Government has held discussions with the State 
Governments regarding the implementation of the Urban Challenge 
Fund and if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE

(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (c):  The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has launched

UCF has been introduced to catalyse a paradigm shift in urban development 
by encouraging cities to transition towards market -based financing and 
integrated regional development. The Fund aims to position cities as a

Under UCF, private sector participation is governed by the respective

AGRO PROCESSING CLUSTERS IN UTTAR PRADESH 
  
813.  SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA: 
SHRI LALJI VERMA: 
MRS RUCHI VIRA: 
SHRI NEERAJ MAURYA: 
             
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether a number of approved 'Agro Processing Clusters' in Uttar Pradesh particularly 
Etah and Kasganj have been limited to function only as 'cold storage' units and processing 
work therein has not started yet in the absence of technical experts, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b)  whether the cold chain operations have turned expensive due to erratic power supply in 
several areas of Uttar Pradesh including the eastern and Bundelkhand regions, Etah and 
Kasganj forcing small farmers to sell their produce at throwaway prices instead of being 
able to properly and safely store the same, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the local entrepreneurs in Uttar Pradesh including Etah and Kasganj are facing 
huge bureaucratic hurdles and complex paperwork in getting 'bank loans' for setting up 
Agro Processing Units despite a nationally allocated budget of Rs. 6,520 crore, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d)  the details of 'Agro Clusters' that have been physically created but are currently not 
operational with any farmer group or startup? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a 
Scheme for Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC), a component 
scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) since 2017. The scheme aims 
to develop modern infrastructure with certain capital-intensive facilities like cold storages, 
blast freezers, specialized packaging, IQF, warehousing etc., for encouraging entrepreneurs to 
set up food processing units based on the cluster approach. The APC is demand driven scheme 
not State/district specific.  Further, there is no provision for setting up of standalone cold 
storage under the APC scheme. As on date, there is no project approved in Etah and Kasganj 
districts in the State of Uttar Pradesh under APC scheme. However, Ministry has approved two 
agro processing clusters in the State of Uttar Pradesh under the scheme, which have been 
completed. The details of these two projects is attached as Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO: 816 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY 2026 
  
OPERATION GREENS 
  
816. SHRI BRIJMOHAN AGARWAL: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the budget allocated and actual expenditure utilized for the Short-Term 
Interventions component of Operation Greens in 2025-26 and 2026-27 till date;  
(b) whether retrospective Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) data severely 
delays the Trigger Price Mechanism, causing Farmer Producer Organisation (FPOs) to 
face distress sales before transport and storage subsidies are officially activated and if 
so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of FPOs from Chhattisgarh’s aspirational districts that successfully claimed 
this fifty per cent subsidy during recent tomato and minor fruit price crashes; and 
(d) the corrective measures proposed, such as integrating the SAMPADA portal with real-
time e-NAM APIs for predictive advance subsidy alerts or providing upfront subsidy 
vouchers instead of delayed reimbursements? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a) to (d): Under short term interventions component of Operation Greens scheme, the Ministry 
of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) was providing transportation and storage subsidy for 
eligible perishable crops @50% of eligible cost. However, the same was transferred to 
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) in 2023-24. Hence, no budget has 
been allocated to MoFPI for the short-term interventions’ component of Operation Greens in 
2025-26 and 2026-27. 
Investment & Price Support Division under DA&FW deals with the implementation of 
Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) under the integrated Scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata 
Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) for the procurement of agricultural and horticultural 
commodities which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the MSP regime. The 
sanction details under MIS since 2025-26 to 2026-27 (as on 17.07.2026) is given in 
the Annexure. 
  
The objective of MIS is to protect the growers from making distress sale in the event 
of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall below economic 

levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent decrease in the ruling 
market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request of a 
State/UT government, which is ready to bear 50 percent of the loss (25 percent in case of North-
Eastern States), if any, incurred on its implementation. The extent of total amount of loss to be 
shared on a 50:50 basis between the Central Government and the State Government is restricted 
up to 25 percent of the total procurement value based on Market Intervention Price (MIP) which 
includes cost of the commodity procured plus permitted overhead expenses. The total 
procurement value is the cost of procured quantity at Market Intervention Price (MIP) 
determined by MIS Committee plus permitted overheads expenses, which is generally of 25% 
of MIP. Under this scheme, the procurement is carried out by State designated agency upto 
25% of estimated state production of the particular crop at fixed MIP. However, States/UTs 
have also an option to make the differential payment between the MIP and Sale Price to the 
farmers without physical procurement.  
  
Further, in special cases, where there is a price difference of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion 
and Potato) between the producing and consuming states, in the interest of the farmers, the 
operational costs incurred by Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) like National Agricultural 
Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and National Cooperative 
Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF) and State designated agencies in storing and 
transporting crops from the producing state to other consuming states will be reimbursed.

entries.t: Edible Oil Extraction and Processing Capacity
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 817 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
  
EDIBLE OIL EXTRACTION AND PROCESSING CAPACITY  
  
817. SHRI RAJEEV RAI: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to enhance domestic edible oil extraction 
and processing capacity and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of oilseed processing units established or modernised during the last three 
years; and 
(c) whether financial assistance has been extended for value addition and processing 
infrastructure and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
 
(a):       As informed by Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture 
& Farmers Welfare, the Union Cabinet approved the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds 
(NMEO-OS) on 3rd October, 2024 with an outlay of Rs. 10,103.38 crore (Central share of Rs 
7,481.67 crore) to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive toward self-sufficiency in 
edible oils.  The Mission aims to increase primary oilseed production to 69.7 million tonnes, 
expand area coverage to 33 million hectares, and improve productivity to 2,112 kg/ha by 2030-
31. 
The Mission is being implemented in a cluster-based approach with market linkage. 
Value Chain Clusters are managed by Value Chain Partners such as Farmer Producer 
Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under these clusters, farmers are 
provided free high-quality seeds upto area of 1 hectare each and training on good agricultural 
practices. In addition, assistance is also provided for Machinery & Equipment for Oil extraction 
units (10 tonne capacity) and processing of oilseeds @ 33% of the project cost upto a maximum 
of Rs 9.90 lakh per unit to improve the capacity & efficiency of edible oil production. So far, 
l3.52 lakh hectares have been covered under free seed distribution in the Value Chain Clusters 
during 2025-26, against the annual target of 10.00 lakh hectares. In addition, 60 Seed Hubs, 50 
specialized seed storage units and 400 Oil Mills were sanctioned under NMEO Oilseeds during 
2025-26.  
A Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely, National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm 
(NMEO-OP) has been launched during August, 2021 with the aim to enhance the edible oils 
availability in the country by harnessing Oil Palm area expansion, increasing Crude Palm Oil 

(CPO) production and to reduce the import burden on edible oils. Currently, there are 27 
operational oil palm processing mills are functioning across the country.  
(b) & (c): Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been supporting setting up/ 
expansion of food processing infrastructure, including edible oil processing units, through its 
two Central Sector Scheme viz. Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), 
Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) and a Centrally 
sponsored PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme across 
the country. 
Schemes implemented by MoFPI aim towards creation of modern infrastructure with 
efficient supply chain management from farm gate to retail outlet which includes storage, 
transportation, value addition etc., thereby enhancing productivity, reducing wastage of 
agricultural produce, reduction in post-harvest losses & increasing the processing level.  
As on 30.06.2026, under Creation / Expansion of Food Processing & Preservation 
Capacities Scheme (CEFPPC), a component scheme of PMKSY, during 2023-24 to 2025-26, 
total 14 projects related to edible oil processing have been approved with grants in aid of Rs 
55.32 crore. Similarly, under PMFME scheme, during 2023-24 to 2025-26, total 10120 micro 
food enterprises related to oil processing have been approved across the country.

entries.t: Implementation of Automated Testing Stations for Vehicle Fitness
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 818 
ANSWERED ON 23rd JULY, 2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF AUTOMATED TESTING STATIONS FOR 
VEHICLE FITNESS 
  
818. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
  
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether  the Government is aware of any challenges faced 
regarding the mandatory rollout of Automated Testing Stations (ATS) 
for vehicle fitness certification, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the limited number of operational centres forces operators 
to travel long distances, causing financial loss and whether steep fee 
structures and high rejection rates for minor technicalities are unfairly 
penalising older commercial vehicles, if so, the details thereof;  
  
(c) whether any State Government has formally requested a temporary 
rollback or a hybrid model to re -enable manual testing alongside 
automated systems to prevent regional transit disruptions, if so, the 
details thereof; and  
  
(d) the  corrective steps being taken by the Government to upgrade 
manual testing centres, subsidise ATS fees and ensure accessible 
fitness certification facilities nationwide? 

  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (c)         The Government in Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways has formulated the Voluntary Vehicle -Fleet Modernization 
Programme (VVMP) which includes a system of incentives and dis -
incentives to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. Und er this 
policy, the Government has notified the rules for recognition, 
regulation and control of automated testing stations vide GSR 
notification 652(E) dated 23.09.2021 (as amended from time to time) to 
test the vehicles for fitness through automated equi pment with 
minimum human intervention. 
  
A notification was issued vide GSR 709(E) dated 14.11.2024 
(amending rule 62 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989) which 
provides for mandatory testing of Transport Vehicles through an 
Automated Testing Station , registered in accordance with rule 175 of 
the Central Motor Vehicle Rules 1989, from 01st April 2025. 
  
         The responsibility of setting up of ATSs lies with the respective 
State Governments. As on 17.07.2026, there are 276 operational ATSs 
in 20 States and Union Territories. The number of ATSs has increased 
substantially in the recent past along with the geographical coverage : 
- 
  
Fiscal Year Total ATSs State/UTs with ATSs 
2022-23 7 3 

2023-24 52 11 
2024-25 123 14 
2025-26 195 20 
2026-27 
(till date) 
276 20 
  
  In accordance with rule 62 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 
1989,the Parivahan  system access for Regional Transport Officers 
(RTOs)/District Transport Officers (DTOs), for conducting manual 
fitness tests and issuing fitness certificates has been revoked based 
on operationalisation of   ATSs in a phased manner. States were also 
communicated that access to manual fitness testing at RTO may be 
reinstated based on request from the State with a time bound plan for 
operationalisation of ATSs.  
In view of the challenges/issues provided by the State 
governments and action plan provided for establishment of ATSs, 
timelines of revocation of manual testing were revised for 
the  following States/UTs,i.e.,Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, 
Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and 
Ladakh. 
         The request for hybrid mode of continuing manual fitness testing 
alongside ATS operations was sent by Government of Himachal 
Pradesh.  Further justification and action plan has been requested 
from the State Government. 
  
(d)    The responsibility of setting up of ATSs lies with  the respective 
State Governments/ Union Territories.However,the Ministry has taken 
various measures to increase the access to ATSs  nationwide, which 
are as follows: 
  

i. Eligibility conditions for owners or operators of ATSs were 
relaxed  vide GSR 349(E) dated 08.05.2026, to increase the pace of 
setting up of ATSs.  
ii. To expedite the setting up of the ATSs, the process of 
application and approval is being done online on National Single 
Window System.   
iii. In order to expand coverage of ATSs, incentives were given to 
the States under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for 
Capital Investment from FY 2022 -23 to FY 2025 -26. The incentives 
were given based on achievements of various milestones by the States 
for setting up of ATSs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 820 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY 2026 
 
FOOD PROCESSING CLUSTER IN UJJAIN 
  
820. SHRI ANIL FIROJIYA: 
             
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) whether the Government proposes to set up a mega food park or food processing cluster 
in the Ujjain Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the Government has any plan to provide special incentives to 
processing industries for agricultural and horticultural produce in the Ujjain region and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government would provide financial assistance for the setting up of cold 
storage and food processing units in Ujjain to ensure remunerative prices for farmers for 
their produce and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to approve new projects in Ujjain Lok Sabha 
Constituency to promote micro and small food processing units and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to implement any special scheme for employment 
generation and development of agro-based industries in the Ujjain region through food 
processing industries and if so, the details thereof? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a) to (e): The Ministry does not set up any Agro Processing Cluster or Mega Food Park on its 
own. The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a Scheme 
for Creation of Infrastructure for Agro Processing Clusters (APC), a component scheme of the 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) for development of modern infrastructure 
to encourage entrepreneurs to set up food processing units based on cluster approach in the 
country since 2017. The objective of the scheme is to reduce the loss of surplus produce and 
add value to the horticultural/ agricultural produce, resulting in increase of income of the 
farmers and create employment at the local level Under the scheme, financial assistance in the 
form of grants-in-aid/subsidy @ 35% of the eligible project cost is provided in General Areas 
and 50% of the eligible project cost in North Eastern States including Sikkim and difficult areas 

including Himalayan States (Himachal Pradesh, J&K & Uttarakhand), notified ITDP areas and 
Islands subject to a maximum of Rs.10.00 crore.  
The Mega Food Park scheme has been discontinued with effect from 01.04.2021. 
For setting up of food processing units in the country, Ministry of Food Processing 
Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a Scheme for Creation/Expansion of Food 
Processing & Preservation Capacities (CEFPPC) under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada 
Yojana (PMKSY). Under the scheme, grants-in-aid @ 35% of the eligible project cost is 
provided in General Areas and 50% of the eligible project cost in North Eastern States 
including Sikkim and Difficult areas including Himalayan States (Himachal Pradesh, J&K & 
Uttarakhand), notified ITDP areas and Islands subject to a maximum of Rs.5.00 crore.  
Both the APC and CEFPPC schemes are demand-driven in nature and are not restricted 
to any specific State or district, and under these schemes, standalone cold storage units are not 
permitted. 
As on date, there is no project approved in Ujjain district in the State of Madhya Pradesh 
under APC or CEFPPC scheme.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.821 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
 
FRAUDULENT CARBON CREDIT TRANSACTIONS 
 
821. SHRI BASAVARAJ BOMMAI: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the specific measures taken/proposed to be taken to pre vent fraudulent 
carbon credit transactions in India's evolving carbon market framework;  
 
(b) the manner in which the Government proposes to balance economic growth 
with carbon reduction targets set for 2027 and 2030;  
 
(c) the mechanisms put/proposed to b e put in place to ensure private sector 
compliance with carbon reduction targets; and  
 
(d) the manner in which the Government proposes to integrate the learnings from 
international best practices discussed at Prakriti 2025 into India's climate policy 
framework? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a): As per Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), notified in June, 2023 (as 
amended), the Grid Controller of India is the registry for the Indian carbon market. 
In order to prevent fraudulent carbon credit transactions, the functions assigned 
to the registry for the Indian carbon market include maintaining secure data base 
and records of all transactions. This registry is also the meta-registry for India.  
 
(b): The m andatory compliance of greenhouse gas emission intensity (GEI) 
targets under CCTS covers only emission intensive industries, designated as 
“Obligated Entities” whose annual energy consumption are above certain 
thresholds. Further, while finalizing the GEI targets for different obligated 
entities, the marginal abatement cost of possible technological measures in the 
units of obligated entities are taken into consideration to ensure that such 
entities are given pragmatic and achievable targets.  
………2.  

 
 
- 2 - 
 
(c): Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has published Detailed Procedure for 
Compliance Mechanism under CCTS in July 2024 which covers comprehensive 
Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) framework to ensure accurate, 
transparent, and credible compliance. An essential aspect of the MRV framework 
is the verification process, which requires annual verification of GHG emissions 
data. Further, the environmental compensation may be levied and penalty may be 
imposed under Environment Protection Act in ca se of non -compliance of GEI 
targets by obligated entities.  
 
(d): During "PRAKRITI" 2025, an international conference on carbon markets, 
industries, financial institutions, and other stakeholders participated in detailed 
deliberations on various aspects of  carbon markets, greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emission reduction measures, financing for clean technologies, and related 
issues. Based on the outcomes of these deliberations, the Government of India is 
taking steps to incorporate international best practices into its climate policies, 
including the establishment of a robust and transparent carbon market and its 
alignment with global policies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 822 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
SAFETY AUDIT OF AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS  
822.    SHRI SHYAMKUMAR DAULAT BARVE       
       
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has conducted a comprehensive safety audit 
regarding the operational risks posed to passengers and flight crew during 
aircraft operations at short -length and table -top runways in the country and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the specific vulnerabilities identified at such airports along 
with the total number of such short -length runways currently operational in the 
country; and 
 
(c) the details of the preventive measures, advanced technological  installations 
and infrastructure expansion plans being implemented by the Government to 
mitigate such risks and ensure maximum safety? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (c): Safety audits are car ried out during Main Base Inspection and Station 
Facility Inspection as per Annual Surveillance Plan for all operators. Periodic 
assessment related to Runway such as Pavement Inspection, Friction Testing, 
Rubber Removal, Pavement marking and lighting check s, Runway Condition 
Reporting (RCR) etc. are conducted at Airports Authority of India (AAI) 
Airports as per DGCA CAR regulations. 
 
Aerodrome operators are required to implement a Safety Management System 
(SMS), maintain Runway End Safety Areas (RESA), ob stacle limitation 
surfaces, rescue and firefighting services (ARFF), aeronautical ground lighting, 
visual aids and emergency response plans in accor dance with the applicable 
CARs. 

 
The following aerodromes are mandatorily classified as Category C requiri ng 
enhanced operational competence: Calicut, Kullu, Leh, Lengpui, Mangalo re, 
Pakyong, Shimla and Thoise. 
 
Further, DGCA has prescribed special operational requirements for operations 
at Cat C aerodromes through Operations Circular No. 02 of 2012 Rev 3 
regarding Route and Aerodrome Competence Qualification, read with CAR 
Section 8, Series O, Part II and Part VII. The Circular requires operators to 
undertake safety risk assessments, classify aerodromes based on operational 
complexity, and prescribe minimum experience, training, assessment and 
qualification requirements for flight crew operating to such aerodromes. 
******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 823 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
RULES FOR GATE NO-SHOW  
823.    SHRI BALASHOWRY VALLABHANENI        
      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the meaning of gate no -show and the manner in which airlines facilitate and 
make efforts to ensure that passengers arrive at the boarding gate before the 
departure of the flight; 
(b) the time fixed for passengers to arrive at the boarding gate before the departure 
of the flight; 
(c) the manner in which gate no-show is different from no-show; and 
(d) whether it is true that different airlines have different rules in their Conditions 
of Carriage with regard to gate no -show and if so, the reasons f or not prescribing 
uniform rules for all airlines in this regard? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): Ministry of Civil Aviation/ DGCA has not issued any specific regulations or 
guidelines defining the terms "no-show" or "gate closure time". 
However, as a standard and globally recognised aviation term, "gate no -show" 
refers to a situation where a passenger has completed check -in but fails to report at 
the boarding gate within the stipulated time and, t herefore, is denied boarding. 
Airlines facilitate timely boarding of passengers through multiple channels, 
including issuance of boarding passes indicating boarding time, announcements at 
the airport, display of flight information on information screens an d, where 
feasible, SMS/e-mail alerts. 
 
(b): While the exact gate closure time may vary depending on the airline, airport, 
and route, airlines communicate the applicable gate closure time to passengers 
through their Conditions of Carriage at the time of boo king, and the same is also 
indicated on the boarding pass. 

 
(c): A no -show refers to a passenger who does not check in or does not present 
himself/herself for travel on the booked flight, whereas as a standard and globally 
recognised aviation term, a gate no-show refers to a passenger who has checked in 
but fails to report at the boarding gate within the prescribed time. 
 
(d): With the repeal of Air Corporations Act in March 1994, Indian domestic 
aviation was totally deregulated. Airlines are permitted to f rame their own 
Conditions of Carriage and fare rules, subject to the applicable regulatory 
framework. 
******

entries.t: Challenges faced by Micro Food Processing Enterprises
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 826 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
  
CHALLENGES FACED BY MICRO FOOD PROCESSING ENTERPRISES 
  
826. SHRI ATUL GARG:  
DR. D. PURANDESWARI:  
SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
  
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has identified implementation challenges faced by micro food  
processing enterprises under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; 
(b) the steps taken to prepare and disseminate model Detailed Project Reports and guide 
prospective entrepreneurs to facilitate seamless processing of applications; 
(c) whether District Resource Persons and Trained Master Trainers have been appointed to 
hand holding applicants and improve sanction rates, if so, the details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefor; 
(d) the measures adopted to expand common facility centres, incubation support and 
partnerships with banks and technical institutes; and 
(e) the manner in which the efforts/initiatives taken under the scheme would strengthen the 
formalisation of micro food processing enterprises, enhance marketability and increase 
rural employment opportunities particularly in Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh), 
Rajahmundry (Andhra Pradesh), Khagaria and Samastipur (Bihar) Lok Sabha 
Constituencies? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
  
(a): The Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) 
Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored, demand-driven Scheme aimed at providing financial, 
technical and business support to micro food processing enterprises. During the course of 
implementation, certain challenges have been observed, including limited awareness among 
beneficiaries, delays in release of the State share, difficulties in obtaining statutory registrations 
and licenses, capacity constraints of micro enterprises, inadequate technology upgradation, 
gaps in project preparation, branding and market linkages, and challenges in meeting 
documentation requirements for food safety compliances. 
 
(b) to (c):  To facilitate preparation of bankable project proposals, 190 Model Detailed Project 
Reports (DPRs) covering various food processing activities have been developed by NIFTEM-
Thanjavur and NIFTEM-Kundli in consultation with technical experts and are available on the 
PMFME portal. Under the Scheme, District Resource Persons (DRPs) have been engaged by 

States/UTs to provide end-to-end handholding support to beneficiaries including project 
identification, preparation of DPRs, online application submission, obtaining statutory 
registrations, coordination with banks and formalisation support. The Scheme has also 
developed a robust capacity-building ecosystem through Master Trainers and District Level 
Trainers (DLT), who impart Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) and product-
specific training to beneficiaries, thereby improving project quality, credit readiness and loan 
sanction rates. 
  
(d): Under the scheme, Support for creation of Common Infrastructure is provided @ 35% 
of eligible project cost with maximum limit of Rs. 3 Crore to Farmer Producer Organizations 
(FPOs)/ Self Help Groups (SHGs) and its Federations/ Cooperatives/ Government Agencies to 
establish food processing line along with common infrastructure/ value chain/ incubation 
centre. The proposals are mobilized and approved by the State Nodal Departments, as per the 
Scheme guidelines.  These shared facilities are aimed at reducing capital costs and promote 
technology adoption.  
The Scheme also provides financial assistance for establishment of Common 
Incubation Centres (CICs) to improve access to modern processing, testing, packaging, storage 
and training infrastructure for micro food processing enterprises. Proposals for establishment 
of CICs are identified and recommended by the States/UTs based on the ODOP and local 
processing requirements, for approval by the Ministry. As on 30th June 2026, 80 incubation 
centres have been approved across 27 States/ UTs.   
In addition to this, State Level Technical Institutes (SLTI) have been identified in each 
of the State for nominating Master Trainers, coordinating and conducting training programmes 
for DRPs and DLTs, translating and adapting training materials into regional languages, 
customizing DPRs to suit State-specific requirements, providing technical guidance to the State 
Nodal Agency (SNA) on food processing matters, and supporting beneficiary handholding 
through capacity building and training for enterprise formalisation.  
Further, all scheduled commercial banks are participating in the Scheme, and regular 
review meetings are held with the State Governments and banking institutions to improve credit 
flow and implementation. Department of Financial Services

Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any adequate funds have been allocated for water conservation schemes in the country, if so, the 
details thereof including utilisation status and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether climate change has aggravated water stress in the country, if so, the details thereof and the 
mitigation strategies adopted in this regard; 
(c) whether the rapid urbanisation has increased pressure on water resources, if so, the details thereof and the 
steps taken thereon; 
(d) whether the Government has promoted efficient water use in agriculture, if so, the details thereof 
including micro-irrigation initiatives and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) whether wastewater treatment and reuse systems have been strengthened, if so, the details thereof 
including the capacity created and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (e)   ‘Water’ being a State subject, the aspects related to water resources including its conservation are 
studied, planned, funded and executed by the State Governments themselves as per their own resources and 
priorities. The Central Government supplements the measures and efforts being taken up by the State 
Governments. 
Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative was launched in Surat, Gujarat on 6 September 2024. In 
June 2025, JSJB 2.0 was launched. The implementation cycle for JSJB 2.0 commenced on 1 June 2025 and 
concluded on 31 May 2026. 
Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB: CTR) – 2026 was launched on 1st June 2026 
enhancing the scope of the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative and simultaneously integrating it with 
the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign. The initiative focuses on intensifying 
community action and mobilization to build low-cost rainwater harvesting structures in low cost and 
saturation mode.  
The initiative leverages community funds, individual donations, Corporate Social Responsibility 
Funds and others for construction of low-cost structures like borewells, recharge shafts, recharge pits, using 
locally available material, to harvest rainwater, to boost ground water level and provide local tailor-made 
solution to water issues. The initiative also emphasizes convergent financing from various schemes of the

Central, State and local bodies like Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) 
(VB-G RAM G), Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), Per Drop More Crop, 
Repair, Renovation and Restoration Components under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 
(PMKSY), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) and Finance 
Commission grants. 
In 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti launched Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA) as a time-bound, mission-mode 
water conservation campaign in 256 water stressed districts of the country. The Hon'ble PM of India 
launched the campaign in 2021 as Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) with the message, "Catch 
the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls." Since then, JSA: CTR evolved into a national movement, 
reinforcing India's collective commitment to water security through localised action and institutional 
convergence. The JSA: CTR campaign was implemented nationwide and each edition had included a 
targeted focus since 2023 to maximize impact. The JSA: CTR 2023, with the theme “Source Sustainability 
for Drinking Water,” prioritized 150 special focus districts identified by the Jal Jeevan Mission. The JSA: 
CTR 2024 campaign, themed “Nari Shakti se Jal Shakti,” was carried out across the country with a special 
focus on 151 districts identified by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB). The JSA: CTR 2025 was 
launched with the theme “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or” emphasizing deeper grassroots 
engagement, inter-sectoral convergence and innovative financing mechanisms with special focus on 148 
districts identified by CGWB.

ROLE OF INTEGRATED COMMAND AND CONTROL CENTRES IN SMART 
CITIES 
 
NO. 828 SHRI KAMAKHYA PRASAD TASA:  
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is  a fact that Integrated Command and Control Centres 
(ICCCs) have an important role in all Smart Cities and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) the current status of operationalis ation of Integrated Command and 
Control Centres (ICCCs) across all Smart Cities; 
(c) the manner in which these IC CCs are being effectively utilis ed for real-
time monitoring and proactive management of urban challenges; and 
(d) the details of the specific data-driven insights from ICCCs being used to 
inform urban planning and policy decis ions aimed at improving overall 
urban resilience and citizens’ quality of life? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a): Yes, the Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) have played 
a crucial role in the implementation of the Smart Cities Mission.  These 
centres play a vital role in urban management by enabling real -time 
monitoring, data-driven decision- making, and integrated service 
delivery across  various sectors such as mobility, water supply, 
sanitation, solid waste management, public safety, etc. 
 
(b): Under the Smart Cities Mission, Integrated Command and Control 
Centres (ICCCs) have been operationalised across all 100 Smart 
Cities. These centres play a vital role in urban management by 
enabling real -time monitoring, data- driven decision- making, and 
integrated service delivery across key sectors such as mobility, water 
supply, sanitation, solid waste management and public safety. 
…2/- 
 
-2- 
(c): ICCCs are functioning as the nerve centers for city operations, 
enabling real -time monitoring, data- driven decision- making and 
proactive management of urban services. These centres  integrate 
data from various urban domains such as traffic management, solid 

waste management, water supply, street lighting, public safety and 
emergency response systems. Key areas where ICCCs are being 
effectively utilised includes Traffic and Mobility Management, Solid 
Waste Management, Emergency and Disaster Response, Citizen 
Grievance Redressal, Public Safety and Surveillance, etc. 
 
(d): The data- driven insights generated by ICCCs are being increasingly 
leveraged to inform urban planning and policy decisions, thereby 
enhancing urban resilience and improving the quality of life for 
citizens. Specific examples include the use of Intelligent Traffic 
Management System (ITMS), Automatic Number Plate Recognition 
(ANPR) for traffic management and enforcement, GPS -based route 
optimisation for efficient solid waste collection, facial recognition 
systems for enhanced public safety and crowd monitoring 
technologies to manage large gatherings and ensure citizen security. 
These tools enable evidence- based governance, improve operational 
efficiency and support proactive decision making at the city level.

entries.t: Grant of ST Status to Tea Tribes in Assam
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 829 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 23/07/2026 
  
GRANT OF ST STATUS TO TEA TRIBES IN ASSAM  
  
829. MD. RAKIBUL HUSSAIN: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to grant Scheduled Tribe (ST) status to the tribes in Assam including 
Adivasi or "Tea Tribes", Chutia, Koch-Rajbongshi, Matak, Moran and Tai-Ahom communities, which has been 
a long-standing demand, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(b) whether the Government has taken any measures to examine the socio-economic conditions of the said tribes 
in Assam, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
  
(a): The proposal for inclusion of Tai Ahom, Chutia, Matak, Moran, Koch-Rajbongshi and Tea Tribes has been 
received from the State Government of Assam. 
Government of India on 15.6.1999 (further amended on 25.6.2002 and 14.9.2022) has laid down the 
modalities for deciding the claims for inclusion in, exclusion from and other modifications in Orders specifying 
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes lists. As per these modalities, proposals are required to be recommended 
and duly justified along with an ethnographic report by the concerned State Government / UT Administration. 
Thereafter, the proposals are required to be concurred with by the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the 
National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) to be considered and legislation amended. All actions on 
the proposals are taken as per these approved modalities. 
(b): The State Government of Assam has informed that:(i) Govt. of Assam has created Matak Autonomous 
Council, Moran Autonomous Council and Kamatapur Autonomous Council, Adivasi Welfare and Development 
Council and Development Councils for Ahom and Chutia community for all-round socio-economic condition 
of these communities. Sufficient fund have been allocated to these Councils in the annual budget for taking up 
development schemes for their community. 
(ii) Taking note of comparative disparity of the community, the state Government has made special reservations 
for these six (6) communities in the educational institutions like Medical, Engineering colleges, University, ITI 
etc. 
(iii) 200 (two hundred) Model Tea Estate High Schools have been sanctioned in different Tea-garden areas to 
meet the aspirations. These schools with state-of-the-art amenities have brought a holistic change among tea 
garden workers and children as far as quality education is concerned. The schools are equipped with modern 
amenities for quality education, efficient teachers, technology, smart classrooms and future prospects and plans 
for the overall development of the students. Out of these, 116 Model Tea Estate High Schools have been made 
fully functional since 2023. Within a span of 2-3 years, these Model Schools shall be upgraded into Higher 
Secondary schools.

Government has undertaken the following initiatives to support Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) and boost their competitiveness and their participation in global value chain: 
-  
 
i. The Export Promotion Mission (EPM) launched in November 2025 seeks to  provide a 
comprehensive, flexible, and digitally driven framework for export promotion, with a total outlay 
of Rs.25,060 crore for FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31. The Mission operates through two integrated 
sub-schemes: 
a. Niryat Protsahan focuses on improving access to affordable trade finance for MSMEs through 
a range of instruments such as interest subvention, export factoring, credit guarantee and 
credit enhancement support for diversification into new markets. 
 

: 2 : 
 
b. Niryat Disha  focuses on non -financial enablers that enhance market readiness and 
competitiveness, including export quality and compliance support, assistance for 
international branding, packaging, and participation in trade fairs, export warehousing and 
logistics, inland tran sport reimbursements, and trade intelligence and capacity -building 
initiatives. 
 
ii. Credit Guarantee Scheme for Exporters has also been approved to provide 100% credit 
guarantee coverage by National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) to 
Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) for extending additional collateral free credit facilities 
up to Rs.20,000 crore to eligible exporters, including MSMEs. The Scheme is expected to 
enhance the global competitiveness of Indian exporters and support diversification  into new 
and emerging markets.  
 
iii. Ministry of Micro, Small  and Medium Enterprises (MSME) implements International 
Cooperation Scheme which is aimed at building capacity of MSMEs by facilitating their 
participation in international exhibitions/fairs/conferences/seminar/buyer-seller meets abroad 
as well as reimbursement of various costs involved including reimbursement of Fee paid on 
Testing & Quality Certification acquired by MSEs to export products. 
 
iv. Further, the Ministry of MSME has established 65 Export Facilitation Centres (EFCs) across 
the country with the aim of providing requisite mentoring and handholding support to MSMEs 
in exporting their products and services. Export Facilitation Centres (EFCs) support MSME 
exporters by prov iding comprehensive assistance through dissemination of information on 
export-related schemes and benefits, training and workshops on export compliance, 
handholding in export documentation and procedures, engagement with industry associations, 
State Governments, and DGFT to facilitate MSMEs. 
 
v. Districts as Export Hubs (DEH): This initiative identifies products with export potential in 
every district to address bottlenecks and link local MSMEs with global value chains.  
 
vi. Trade Connect e -Platform: Trade Connect e -Platform has been launched to provide trade -
related information to Indian exporters particularly MSMEs. This platform also serves as an 
online hub for integrating efforts from the Department of Commerce, Indian Missions abroad, 
Export Promotion Councils, Commodity Boards, and other organisations to deliver 
comprehensive support to Indian exporters. 
 
vii. Government periodically assesses the extent of digital adoption among MSMEs, covering 
aspects such as e -commerce platf orms, digital accounting, supply chain digitization, and 
participation in platforms like the Government e -Marketplace (GeM) and Open Network for 
Digital Commerce (ONDC) through Trade Enablement and Marketing (TEAM) scheme 
through independent evaluation studies.

Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the potential of seabuckthorn and apricot-based value 
addition in the UT of Ladakh, particularly in acetic juice processing and CO₂ -based critical oil 
extraction for nutraceutical and cosmetic applications and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to provide capital subsidy, credit -linked financial 
assistance and other incentives under Micro, Small and Medium En terprises (MSMEs) schemes to 
encourage entrepreneurs to establish such units in Ladakh and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether any technical support, skill development, inc ubation and common processing 
facilities are proposed for MSMEs in this sector and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the steps being taken to promote exports and develop Ladakh as a hub for high -value 
seabuckthorn and apricot-based products? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES  
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
  
(a): Government of India, through the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing 
Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme, being implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, 
has identified Seabuckthorn as the One District One Product (ODOP) for Kargil district and Apricot 
as the ODOP for Leh district in the Union Territory of Ladakh. The Scheme supports establishment 
and upgradation of micro food processing enterprises engaged in processing and value add ition of 
these products, including production of juices, nutraceuticals and other value -added products, 
subject to the Scheme guidelines. 
 
(b): Under the PMFME Scheme, Support to upgrade existing units or setting up of new micro 
units is provided through a  credit linked grant @ 35% with maximum grant of Rs.10 lakh, across

scheme being administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the Khadi and Village

beneficiaries belonging to NER, Hill and border areas and Aspirational district, the MM subsidy is 
35% in rural areas and 25% in urban areas. 16 numbers of micro enterprises have been assisted so

entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 840 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23rd July, 2026 
CARBON CAPTURE, UTILISATION AND STORAGE INITIATIVES  
 
840.  SMT. MAHIMA KUMARI MEWAR:  
 SHRI RAMESH AWASTHI:  
 SHRI MUKESHKUMAR CHANDRAKAANT DALAL: 
 SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA : 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of progress made so far in the implementation of initiatives related to Carbon Capture, 
Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) in the petroleum and natural gas sector;  
(b)  the details of the refineries and upstream projects identified for the implementation of pilot 
projects;  
(c)  the details of incentives and regulatory framework proposed by the Government to encourage 
private investment in CCUS technologies; and  
(d)  the quantum of contribution expected from CCUS in meeting India's climate commitments? 
ANSWER 
पेᮝोिलयम और ᮧाक ृ ितक गैस मंᮢालय मᱶ रा᭔य मंᮢी 
(᮰ी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d)  : The Ministry of Power is the nodal Ministry for the Carbon Capture, Utilisation 
and Storage (CCUS) programme. Various Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in the oil and gas 
sector are undertaking pilot projects and techno-economic feasibility studies for the deployment 
of CCUS technologies across the States of Assam, Gujarat, Haryana, Odisha, Maharashtra, 
Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. These projects cover diverse applications, including 
Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR), production of chemicals, dry ice for the beverage industry etc. 
As part of these initiatives, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) is establishing a 
CO2 capture demonstration unit at the Bina Refinery. Further, the 72 tonnes per day (TPD) CO2 
capture demonstration plant at HPCL's Visakh Refinery has achieved mechanical completion. 
The captured CO2 is proposed to be utilized for the production of beverages. 
 
In line with the CCUS Roadmap launched in December 2025, an outlay of INR 20,000 crore 
has been proposed over a period of five years in the Union Budget 2026–27 for the 
development and deployment of CCUS technologies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 841 
ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
IMPLEMENTATION OF JAL JEEVAN MISSION 2.0 IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
841. SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the status of implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 including the number of rural 
households provided with Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs), households yet to 
be covered along with the funds sanctioned, released and utilised, State-wise; 
(b)  the status of implementation of JJM 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh, district -wise, particularly in 
Palnadu district including the number of households covered and the balance households yet 
to be connected;  
(c) the details of infrastructure gaps identified in Andhra Pradesh under JJM 2.0 and the action 
plan to address them; 
(d) whether any timelines have been fixed for achieving universal household tap water 
coverage in Andhra Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  the steps taken by the Union Government to monitor implementation and ensure timely 
utilisation of funds in the said State?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
(a) to (e) Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) -Har Ghar Jal to enable every rural household including Andhra 
Pradesh, in the country to have assured potable water through tap connection.  The Uni on 
Cabinet has approved extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission, with an enhanced outlay and a 
restructured  reforms in the rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0. 
Drinking water is a State  subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation, and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those 
under the Jal Jeevan Mission, lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The Government 
of India supports the States by providing technical and financial assistance only.  
At the start of the Mission in 2019, only 3.24 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported 
to have tap water connection in the country. As on 20.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural  

Page 2 of 14 
 
households, around 15.89 crore (82.10%) rural households have been provided tap water 
connection. The State -wise details of Household tap water connections (as on 20.07.2026) 
and  financial details (as on 15.07.2026) are at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively.  
In Andhra Pradesh, only 30.74 lakh (32.18%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connection in 2019. As on 20.07.2026, out of 95.53 lakh rural households, around 72.11 lakh 
(75.48%) rural households have been provided tap water conne ction. The details of the status 
of implementation of JJM 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh, district wise (including Palnadu) is at 
Annexure-III. 
As informed by State of Andhra Pradesh, the State has planned for saturation till June 2028 by 
completing all SVS by March 2027, MVS by March 2028, BWS by June 2028 and retrofitting 
by March 2027. The Government of India has Implemented the Comprehensive 
Implementation and Reform Plan (CIRP) for ensuring the comprehensive planning and 
implementation of JJM in the State. 
The Scheme Implementation under JJM 2.0 is being implemented through CIRP and the source 
to tap hydraulic linkages is confirmed by creation of Sujal Gaon Id to ensure functionality of 
schemes throughout the lifecycle, as on 21.07.2026 the State has created 18, 018 Sujal Gaon 
Ids. 
The monitoring of schemes under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 is being carried out through 
the Project Monitoring Module (PMM) of the Sujalam Bharat App to enable monitoring, 
verification, and timely completion of works.

entries.t: Implementation of PM Van Dhan Yojana
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 842 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 23/07/2026 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF PM VAN DHAN YOJANA 
842.     DR. D. PURANDESWARI: 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana has systematically transformed the 
tribal economy by monetizing Minor Forest Produce (MFP) in the Rajahmundry Lok 
Sabha Constituency, if so, the details thereof; 
b) the total number of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras established and operated by local tribal women 
self-help groups in the said region during 2025-26; 
(c) whether the provision of free modern processing toolkits has enabled artisans to add commercial 
value to products such as honey and tamarind, thereby increasing their incomes, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) the details of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) interventions undertaken to protect tribal 
gatherers from financial exploitation by local middlemen; and 
(e) the future steps planned to facilitate direct market linkages for processed forest products by 
onboarding local tribal cooperatives onto major national e-commerce platforms?         
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (TRIBAL AFFAIRS) 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support for establishment of Van Dhan 
Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) through Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India 
Limited (TRIFED) under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) and Pradhan Mantri 
Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha AbhiyaN (PM-JANMAN). A total 114 VDVKs (110 under PMJVM and 
4 under PM JANMAN) have been sanctioned in Rajahmundry Lok Sabha Constituency, covering parts 
of Eluru, East Godavari and Kakinada districts. These VDVKs have facilitated value addition and 
marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP), thereby improving the incomes and livelihoods of tribal 
households. The 110 PMJVM VDVKs are operated through 120 tribal Self-Help Groups (SHGs) 
comprising about 3,600 members, predominantly women. Further, 4 PM JANMAN VDVKs involve 
20 SHGs with 200 PVTG members. However, no new VDVKs were established in the region during 
2025-26. 
(c): Under the Van Dhan initiative, eligible VDVKs have been provided with modem processing 
toolkits and basic infrastructure for value addition or MFPs such as honey, tamarind, turmeric, and 
other forest produce. These facilities have improved product quality, enhanced price shelf life, and 
enabled production of marketable value-added products, resulting in better realization and increased 
income for tribal artisans and SHG members. These VDVKs have generated income of ₹508.80 lakh 
through sales for their tribal members in the State of Andhra Pradesh. 

(d): Under the PMJVM scheme the Ministry of Tribal Affairs notifies Minimum Support Price (MSP) 
for 87 Minor Forest Produce (MFP) items, applicable across all states, including Andhra Pradesh. The 
State Implementing Agencies (SIAs) are provided with revolving funds for procurement of MFPs from 
ST MFP gatherers at the notified MSP in case the market price of MFPs falls below the notified MSP 
thereby providing a safety net for their efforts in MFP collection. Till date, the Ministry of Tribal Affair 
has released an amount of Rs 828.75 lakh to SIA-Girijan Cooperative Corporation, Vizag for 
procurement of MFPs covered under the scheme through which the SIA has procured MFPs of the 
value of Rs 2,056.59 lakh from ST MFP gatherers in the state of Andhra Pradesh.  
(e): The Government proposes to strengthen market access by expanding value addition and branding 
of Forest Produce through VDVKs, strengthening marketing support through TRIFED and State 
Implementing Agencies, establishing buyer-seller linkages, participation in exhibitions and onboarding 
VDVK products on ONDC and TribesIndia.com platforms. 
  
*****
