908.  Smt. PRIYANKA GANDHI VADRA: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any action to address the unsustainable extraction of groundwater  in 
the country and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of over-exploited, critical and semi-critical groundwater blocks, State-wise; 
(c) whether the impact of excessive groundwater ext raction has been assessed and if so, the details th ereof 
including the details of land subsidence, State-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has taken any initiative s to reduce dependence on groundwater extraction, 
especially in agriculture and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the action taken to accelerate groundwater rech arge, especially through restoration and rejuvenati on of 
natural ecosystems such as wetlands? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) & (b)    Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country ar e assessed jointly by the Central Ground 
Water Board and the concerned State Governments/Uni on Territory. As per the National Compilation of 
Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India, 2025, the total Annual Ground Water Recharge has been 
assessed as 448.52 Billion Cubic Metres (BCM), the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource as 407.75 
BCM and the total Annual Ground Water Extraction as 247.22 BCM. The Stage of Ground Water Extraction, 
which represents the ratio of annual groundwater ex traction to annual extractable groundwater resource , has 
been assessed as 60.63 per cent. Agriculture use ac counts for about 87 per cent of the total annual 
groundwater extraction. 
Out of 6,762 assessment units in the country, which  are generally Blocks/Taluks/Mandals/Tehsils, 
730 assessment units have been categorised as Over- exploited, 201 as Critical, 758 as Semi-critical, 4 ,946 as 
Safe and 127 as Saline. The State/UT-wise details of assessment units categorized as Over-exploited, Critical 
and Semi-critical are given at Annexure.  
Comparison of the assessments for 2017 and 2025 ind icates an overall improvement in the 
groundwater-resource scenario. The total Annual Gro und Water Recharge increased from 431.86 BCM in 
2017 to 448.52 BCM in 2025. During the same period,  the Stage of Ground Water Extraction declined from  
63.33 % to 60.63 %, the proportion of Safe assessme nt units increased from about 63 % to 73.14 % and t he 
proportion of Over-exploited assessment units declined from about 17 % to 10.80 %. 

2 
 
The Government has taken a multi-pronged approach t o address unsustainable groundwater 
extraction. The Central Ground Water Authority regu lates groundwater extraction by industries, mining and 
infrastructure projects in 19 States/UTs, in accord ance with the Guidelines dated 24 September 2020, a s 
amended from time to time. Remaining 17 States/UTs have their own groundwater extraction regulatory 
mechanism. The Central Ground Water Board undertake s periodic groundwater-resource assessment, 
groundwater-level monitoring, aquifer mapping and p reparation of aquifer-management plans. Measures 
such as rainwater harvesting, artificial recharge, restoration of water bodies, micro-irrigation, crop  
diversification, water budgeting and community-led groundwater management are also promoted through 
programmes including Jal Shakti Abhiyan, Atal Bhuja l Yojana, Per Drop More Crop and Jal Sanchay Jan 
Bhagidari. As water is a State subject, these efforts supplement the measures taken by the State Governments 
for sustainable groundwater management. 
(c) Land subsidence is a localized phenomenon governed by geological, geotechnical, hydrogeological and 
anthropogenic factors. In susceptible aquifer syste ms, sustained groundwater withdrawal may lead to 
compaction of aquifer material and may contribute t o land subsidence. Scientific institutions have rep orted 
localized subsidence in certain parts of the countr y. However, Ministry has not undertaken comprehensi ve 
State-wise assessment attributing land subsidence exclusively to excessive groundwater extraction. 
(d) & (e)  Water being a State subject, sustainable development and management of groundwater resources is 
primarily the responsibility of the State Governmen ts. However, the Central Government supplements the  
efforts of the State Governments by providing techn ical guidance, policy support and financial assista nce 
through various schemes and programmes. The major i nitiatives taken to regulate groundwater extraction ,

DILAPIDATED CONDITION OF ROAD IN NASHIK

Will the MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)     whether the Government is aware of the dilapidated condition of 
the roads connecting Shirdi, Shani Shingnapur  and Nashik and has taken 
any corrective action in view of the Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027; 
  
(b) whether any road construction proposal from Padhegaon to Shani 
Shingnapur and Khadaka Fata to Khamgaon is under consideration, if so, 
the details thereof; 
  
(c) whether priority would be given to the construction of the 
Baherwadi-Khala Kimri bridge over the Godavari River, which connects 
major pilgrimage sites, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(d) whether immediate sanction would be given to these projects 
under the Central Road Fund (CRF), if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(e) whether any special time -bound plan has been prepared to 
complete these works before the Kumbh Mela, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (e) In view of the upcoming Nashik Kumbh Mela, 2027, the 
Government has sanctioned 16 projects costing Rs. 8500 crores for the 
development of various National Highways (NHs) connecting  Shirdi, 
Shani Shingnapur and Nashik. These projects are under various stages of 
implementation.

these projects fall on the District Roads, the development and 
maintenance of which is the responsibility of State Government of 
Maharashtra. The role of Central Government is limited to approval of list 
of projects prioritised by State Governments/ UTs for development of 
State / UT Roads as per guidel ines for sanction and implementation of 
projects under Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF). Such list of 
projects prioritised and submitted by State / UT Government is 
scrutinized and approved vis -à-vis accrual of the State / UT and 
outstanding committed liabilities of already sanctioned works i.e. Bank 
of Sanction (BOS) under CRIF. As on date, no such proposal for 
development of above roads has been recommended by the State 
Government under CRIF.

entries.t: Expansion of UDAN Scheme in Kerala
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 917 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF UDAN SCHEME IN KERALA  
917.    SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN                   
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the UDAN 
Scheme in Kerala to improve regional air connectivity and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of routes sanctioned, operationalised and discontinued under the 
UDAN Scheme in Kerala during the last three years; 
(c) whether any proposals have been received from the State Government of 
Kerala for inclusion of additional destinations under future phases of the UDAN 
Scheme and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken to improve affordable air connectivity and passenger services in 
underserved regions? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d):  Under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN, one airport in  
Keralam, namely Kannur, has been identified for operationalisation of RCS flight 
services to enhance regional air connectivity. A total of 20 routes have been 
operationalised under RCS-UDAN scheme in Keralam out of which, 12 routes are 
currently operational. 
 
As next phase of UDAN scheme, the Government has launched the Modified 
UDAN Scheme on 04.07.2026 to further enhance regional air connectivity across 
the country, including Kerala, targeting 120 new unserved and underserved 
destinations and facilitating air travel for 4 crore passengers over the next 10 years. 
The Scheme envisages a Challenge Mode framework for the development of 
airports nominated by States. 

 
The UDAN Scheme promotes affordable air travel by providing financial 
incentives to sel ected airline operators (SAOs) through concessions extended by 
the Central Government, State Governments, Union Territories, and airport 
operators to reduce operational costs, along with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) for 
the operation of RCS routes. Further,  selected airline operators are required to 
provide around 50% of the seats as RCS seats, with the applicable airfare capped 
for seats supported through VGF. 
 
******

COLLATERAL FREE CREDIT TO MSEs 
 
918.  SHRI SELVAM G: 
SHRI C N ANNADURAI:  
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) implemented through the Credit Guarantee 
Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) has facilitated collateral -free credit to 
Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the number of MSEs in Tamil Nadu that have received credit guarantees under the scheme 
since 2022, along with the amount sanctioned, district-wise and sector-wise; 
 
(c) whether first -generation entrepreneurs, women -led enterprises and units in backward 
districts of Tamil Nadu have been able to access the benefit of the scheme adequately and if so, the 
assessment by the Government thereof; 
 
(d) whether any complaints regarding delays, high processing charges or reluctance of banks to 
extend collateral-free loans have been received from MSEs in Tamil Nadu and if so, the details 
thereof; and  
 
(e) the corrective measures taken to improve credit flow and enhance awareness of the 
CGTMSE scheme among MSMEs in Tamil Nadu?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (c):  The Ministry of M icro, Small and Medium Enterprise (M SME) implements Credit 
Guarantee Scheme (CGS) for Micro Small Enterprises (MSEs) through Credit Guarantee Fund 
Trust for Mic ro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) to provide credit guarantees for the credit 
facilities extended to MSEs, including first -generation entrepreneurs, women -led enterprises, and 
units located in backward districts, without collateral security or third -party guarantees, across the 
Country, including in Tamil Nadu. 
 
Since its inception in 2000 until 30.06.2026, a total of 10.84 lakh credit guarantees 
amounting to Rs. 1.08 lakh crore have been extended to MSEs in Tamil Nadu, including first -
generation entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises, and units located in backward districts.  
 
District-wise and sector-wise details of guarantees extended to MSEs in Tamil Nadu since 
FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 under the CGS are given in Annexure-I and Annexure-II, respectively. 
 
 

 
: 2 : 
 
 
(d) and (e):  The details of the measures taken by the Government to improve credit flow and 
enhance awareness of the CGTMSE scheme among MSEs are given below: 
i. The guarantee ceiling for the loan extended under CGS was enhanced from Rs. 5 crore to 
Rs. 10 crore w.e.f 01.04.2025. 
ii. Annual Guarantee Fee s (AGF) structure revised with 50% reduction in standard rate to as 
low as 0.37% per annum.  
iii. Enhanced extent of guarantee for MSEs led by special category including women led MSEs.  
iv. As per  Reserve Bank of India’s Master Direction - Lending to Micro, Small & Medium 
Enterprises (MSME) Sector  dated 09.02.2026 , all Scheduled Commercial Banks are 
mandated not to accept collateral security in the case of loans up to Rs.20 lakh extended to 
units in the MSE sector. 
v. To promote credit flow to MSEs in Identified Credit Deficient Districts (ICDD) as per RBI, 
CGTMSE offers 10% discount on the AGF and extend an additional 5% guarantee 
coverage.  
vi. To provide enhanced guarantee coverage for credit facilities extended by Memb er Lending 
Institutions (MLIs) to the MSEs engaged in Manufacturing Sector situated in the State of 
Tamil Nadu, a special guarantee scheme “Tamil Nadu Credit Guarantee Scheme (TNCGS)”  
in collaboration with Government of Tamil Nadu is being implemented.  
vii. The performance of banks under the CGTMSE Scheme and the overall flow of credit to the 
MSME sector are reviewed periodically in the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) 
meetings. 
viii. Ministry of MSME, through its field offices, regularly organizes outreach prog rammes in 
coordination with MSME/ Industry Departments of States/UTs concerned and other 
stakeholders like CGTMSE, SIDBI, SLBC, Banks, MSME Associations etc., to create 
awareness of the Scheme.

923. Kumari Sudha R: 
 Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
(a) whether AYUSH subjects proposed to be integrated with allopathic MBBS 
Curriculum have been implemented, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether AYUSH medicines are included in the approved list of medicine for 
reimbursement under health insurance scheme, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether AYUSH practitioners are included in medical boards of various centrally -
run institutions to certify injuries and percentage of disability for Motor Accident Claims

(a)  As per Competency Based Medical Education Curriculum, 2024, framed by the National 
Medical Commission under "New teaching/learning elements" it is mentioned that during

i.e. Ayush in India and history of medicine.

reimbursement under health insurance schemes. The admissibility of reimbursement for 
AYUSH medicines is governed by the terms and conditions of the respective health

applicable regulatory provisions. Accordingly, the list of reimbursable Ayush medicines, if 
any, may vary from insurer to insurer and from one insurance product to another. 
(c) The Ministry of Ayush does not maintain information regarding the inclusion of AYUSH 
practitioners in Medical Boards for certifying injuries and assessment of percentage of 
disability for Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT). However, the National 

Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Ethics and Registration) Regulations, 2023  
and the National Commission for Homoeopathy (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Code 
of Ethics for Practitioners of Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2022 , notified by the National 
Commission for Indian System of Medicine and the  National Commission for 
Homoeopathy, respectively, permit registered Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa -Rigpa and 
Homoeopathy  practitioners to issue medical certificates and others certificate in accordance 
with the applicable regulations. 
(d) Complaints regarding Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Sowa -Rigpa and Homoeopathy 
colleges are received from time to time and are examined by the respective statutory

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 24TH JULY,2026
FUNCTIONAL DIALYSIS UNITS IN PUBLIC HOSPITALS
924. SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ:
ADV PRIYASAROJ:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of dialysis units sanctioned for Government hospitals under Centrally
Sponsored health schemes in the country during the last five years, State-wise, particularly
for Uttar Pradesh;
(b) the number of such units reported as functional on Central monitoring portals as on
January 2026, State-wise and district-wise, particularly for Uttar Pradesh;
(c) the number of sanctioned units flagged in Central reviews as non-operational for more
than three consecutive months, State-wise, particularly for Uttar Pradesh;
(d) whether Central Management Information Systems (MIS) and review reports capture
reasons for non-functionality, including equipment downtime, manpower gaps, or contractual
issues if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether it is a fact that a standard Central reporting protocol exists to distinguish
sanctioned, installed, and operational dialysis capacity under these schemes, if so, the details
thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) ‘Public Health’ and ‘Hospitals’ are state subjects. However, the Government of India
provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs under the National Health Mission
(NHM) for strengthening healthcare infrastructure, including dialysis services.
Under NHM, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the Pradhan Mantri
National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP) in 2016 to improve access to haemodialysis services
by establishing dialysis centres in District Hospitals across the country and providing free
dialysis services to eligible patients. Under the Programme, the Ministry provides financial
assistance to the States/UTs for establishment of dialysis centres based on the proposals
submitted by them under their annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs), prepared on
the basis of gap analysis.
The Programme is presently being implemented in all 36 States/UTs covering 751 districts
(including 44 linked districts) through 1,856 haemodialysis centres equipped with 13,535
haemodialysis machines, as reported by the States/UTs as on 30.06.2026. The number of
dialysis units established at the Government Hospitals under PMNDP for the last five years,
State/UTs wise is placed as Annexure I.

(b) As per the PMNDP monitoring portal, the State/UT-wise details of districts where
dialysis centres are functional and non-functional are at Annexure-II. In the State of Uttar
Pradesh, dialysis centres are functional in all 75 districts.
(c) and (d) The Ministry undertakes periodic monitoring of the Programme through the
Common Review Mission (CRM) and review visits by senior officers. During such reviews,
non-operational dialysis centres, if any, are brought to the notice of the concerned State/UT
for taking corrective action. The responsibility for ensuring continuous functionality of
dialysis centres rests with the respective State/UT Government and the implementing partner,
wherever engaged. The PMNDP IT Portal captures programme implementation and service
delivery parameters through a standardized reporting mechanism; however, it does not
capture specific reasons for non-functionality such as equipment downtime, manpower
shortages or contractual issues, which are monitored by the respective State/UT Governments.
(e) A standardized reporting mechanism has been established under the Pradhan Mantri
National Dialysis Programme (PMNDP), through which States/UTs report information on
dialysis centres established, haemodialysis machines installed and operational status on the
PMNDP IT Portal for monitoring of the Programme.

Mission Shakti comprises of two verticals 'sambal' for safety and security of women and

One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical under the umbrella Mission Shakti. 
It provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women affected

Women Helpline (181) provides 24-hour toll-free telecommunication services to support women 
in both emergency and non-emergency situations. Since inception till 30th June, 2026, over 1.04

assisted in the State of Odisha, 10.34 lakhs women assisted in the State of Uttar Pradesh and 4.44 
lakhs women assisted in the State of Maharasht ra through Women Helpline. The number of 

women beneficiaries assisted through OSCs is at Annexure-I and Women Helplines is at

of activities under the scheme and reviews status of achievement of objectives, effective delivery

the scheme through meetings, video conferencing and by making field visits to States/UTs from

through participation in public events such as trade fairs, marathons, medical conferences,
technology events, encouraging the creation of ABHA and the adoption of digital healthcare.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

 929. SMT. LOVELY ANAND: 
  
  Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the current status of implementation of the Anganwadi -cum-Creche (cradle home)/Palna 
Scheme, Palan Ghar and Working Women's Hostel schemes approved under Mission 
Shakti including the approved/operational units in Bihar, district-wise; 
(b)  whether any special training/evaluation system has been implemented in the said State to 
improve the efficiency, capacity building, digital monitoring and quality of service of the 
staff of Women Helpline-181 and One Stop Centres; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the details of the steps being taken by the Government to effectively provide immediate 
legal, medical and psychosocial counselling as well as shelter and rehabilitation services, 
to women in situations of violence and crisis? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (d):    Palna Scheme:  The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) under 
Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure 
environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their 
employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, 
growth monitoring, immunization, education etc.  Palna component under Samarthya vertical of 
Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme and is implemented with a funding  ratio of 60:40 
between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & Special 
Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding is provided by 
the Central Government. Palna is a demand driven centrally sponsored scheme and the States/UTs 
assess their requirement and proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) 
after discussion with States/UTs. In State of Bihar, 504 AWCCs are approved and all are 

functional. District wise details of Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) operational in the State of 
Bihar is at Annexure. 
  
Sakhi Niwas Scheme: Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the overarching 
Mission Shakti, is a demand driven Centrally Sponsored Scheme, under which funds are released 
directly to the States/UTs for implementation of the scheme. The States/UTs as sess their 
requirement as per local needs and proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board 
(PAB) after discussion with States/UTs. The scheme aims to promote availability of safe and 
conveniently located accommodation for working women in urban, semi-urban and also in rural 
areas where employment opportunity for women exists. 
Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running of Sakhi Niwas in rented premises 
for working women and for those women who are under training for job. Provision of Day Care 
Centre for children of the residents of the Sakhi Niwas is an impor tant aspect of the scheme.   In 
this scheme, fund is provided for rental accommodation.   Component of construction  has been 
discontinued.  
  
Presently, 575 Sakhi Niwas are functional across the country, including three (03) Sakhi Niwas in 
Bihar, one each located in the districts of Patna, Muzaffarpur and Gaya. 
  
Shakti Sadan Scheme: Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile schemes of ‘Swadhar 
Greh’ – Home for women in difficult circumstances and ‘Ujjawala’ - Home for women rescued 
from Trafficking, have been merged w.e.f. 01.04.2022 and are now known as ‘S hakti Sadan 
Scheme’, which is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for women in distressful

clothing, counselling, legal aid, primary health facilities and other daily requirements. The

BAN ON FIXED DOSE COMBINATIONS (FDCs)
930: THIRU THANGA TAMILSELV AN:
DR. GANAPATHYRAJKUMAR P:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has recently issued notifications under Section 26A of the Drugs
and Cosmetics Act, 1940, prohibiting sixteen more Fixed Dose Combinations (FDCs),
including dermatological preparations, painkillers, antispasmodics and antibiotics;
(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the specific reasons, expert evaluations and the
objective behind banning these sixteen FDCs;
(c) the total number of FDCs banned by the Union Government during the last three years,
year-wise;
(d) the exact date on which these prohibition notifications came into force across the country;
(e) the supervisory and regulatory mechanisms established by the Central and State drug
regulatory authorities to enforce the ban and monitor the manufacture, distribution and retail
sale of these 16 FDCs; and
(f) whether the Government proposes to review more existing FDCs in the near future, if so,
the details and timeframe thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (f): There are provisions under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, under which
Central Government may regulate, restrict or prohibit manufacture, of any drug including
Fixed Dose Combination (FDCs) drugs in public interest if the use of drugs is likely to
involve any risk to human beings or animals or there is no therapeutic justification for the
ingredients contained in FDCs.
The Central Government has prohibited manufacture, sale or distribution of 16 FDCs
vide gazette notification dated 11.06.2026 vide S.O No. 3068(E) to 3083(E) with immediate
effect in public interest under section 26A of Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 in the country.

The details thereof, along with the specific reasons are available on the website of CDSCO i.e.
https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/system/modules/CDSCO.WEB/elements/download_fi
le_division.jsp?num_id=MTQzOTc=
The details of the FDCs prohibited during the last three years are as under.
(i) 14 FDCs vide gazette notification SO no. 2394(E) to 2407(E) dated 02.06.2023,
(ii) 156 FDCs vide gazette notification S.O No. 3285(E) to 3440(E) dated 02.08.2024,
(iii) The fixed dose combination of S(+) Etodolac + Paracetamol vide gazette notification
S.O. 3284(E) dated 12.08.2024.
The prohibitions become effective across the country from the date of publication of the
respective notifications in the Official Gazette.
Manufacture, sale and distribution of prohibited/banned drugs is a punishable offence
under Section 18 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the State Licensing Authorities
are empowered to take action in this regard. As and when any such complaints/issues is
received, the matter is taken up with the concerned State Licensing Authority for necessary
action including the cancellation of the manufacturing licenses.
The meetings of Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC), a statutory committee under the
said Act, comprising of all States /UTs Drugs Controllers as members, are held and various
issues related manufacturing, sale and distribution of drugs are discussed/deliberated and
decisions are taken for effective & uniform implementation of the various provisions of said
Act & Rules.

935. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that the buildings and basic infrastructure of centrally
funded Dr. Radhakrishnan Government Medical College at Jolsappar, Nadaun, Hamirpur
district, Himachal Pradesh have been ready for nearly two years, yet MBBS classes, OPD
services have not started;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for the inordinate delay in commencing
the academic session, hospital services in this regard;
(c) whether the Government has requested the State Government of Himachal Pradesh to
issue the necessary permissions and complete the formalities for the operationalisation of the
college and the attached hospital;
(d) if so, the details of correspondence and meetings held between the Central and State
Governments on this issue during the last two years;
(e) the steps taken/being taken by the Union Government to remove the bottlenecks and
ensure early operationalisation of the medical college; and
(f) the details of the tentative timeline by which the college will commence MBBS classes
and OPD services?

THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (f): The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare administers a Centrally Sponsored
Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new medical colleges attached with existing
district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and aspirational districts,
where there is no existing Government or private medical college. The fund sharing
mechanism between the Centre and State Governments is in the ratio of 90:10 for North

Eastern and Special Category States, and 60:40 for others. Under the Scheme, all the
envisaged 157 medical colleges have been approved in three phases, including 03 medical
colleges in Himachal Pradesh at Chamba, Hamirpur and Nahan. All the three medical

Centre and State Government in the ratio of 90:10. Entire Central Share of Rs.170.10 crore

2018-19 with an intake capacity of 100 MBBS seats, and OPD services also commenced
during the same academic year. Subsequently, the intake capacity has been increased to 120
MBBS seats. Further, as per guidelines of the Scheme, the planning, execution and
commissioning of the medical colleges approved under the scheme is to be done by the State

(b) if so, the details thereof, including the regulatory body responsible for enforcement and
the penalties prescribed for violation;
(c) whether those guidelines cover unqualified individuals posing as health experts, if so,

medical advice being circulated on social media by unqualified individuals and if so, the
details of complaints registered along with the action taken during the last five years in

delivery of quality patient care, observance of confidentiality and professional discretion,

SHRI N K PREMACHANDRAN:
THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN:
SHRI K C VENUGOPAL:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the performance of Passport Offices and Passport Seva Kendras 
across the country, particularly in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) whether recently the Government has increased the fees for

years and reasons for the increase;

individual or tourist’s association to reduce fee/consider withdrawing 
it, if so, the response of the Government thereto; and

revenue expected annually due to this recent fee hike ?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) Passport Offices and Passport Seva Kendras continue to provide  
passport services efficiently across the country. In Andhra Pradesh,

review  of  the  cost  of  providing  passport  and  related  services, 
operational requirements, and service delivery improvements. Earlier,  
passport fees were revised in 1971, 1980, 1993, 2002, 2012, and now

passport services including implementation of upgraded Passport Seva

passport fees collected goes to the Consolidated Fund of India.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 939 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 24TH JULY, 2026 
 
REVIEW OF THE PENDENCY OF CASES IN COURTS 
 
939. DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO: 
 
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any review of the pendency of cases in various 
courts across the country, including High Courts and District Courts, if so, the details thereof, 
and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) the present status of implementation of digital judicial infrastructure under the e -Courts 
Project Phase-III; 
(c) the details of funds allocated and released under the project during the last three years, 
State/UT-wise; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to reduce judicial delays and improve access to justice 
through technology and judicial reforms?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
 
(a) to (d):  Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the judiciary. 
However, the Government is fully committed to speedy disposal of cases and reducing 
pendency. The Government has taken several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for fast er 
disposal of cases by the judiciary which, inter -alia, includes amalgamation of latest 
technologies under the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, better infrastructure for courts, policy 
and legislative measures in the areas prone to excessive litigation. 
 
The Phase-III of the eCourts Project (2023 -2027) was approved on 13.09.2023 with an 
outlay of Rs.7,210 crore. Phase III envisions a transition towards digital, paperless courts 
through large -scale digitisation of records, wider use of virtual hearings, interoperability 
across institutions and adoption of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence 
(AI), analytics and Optical Character Recognition (OCR). The current status of progress made 
under eCourts Phase-III is as under: 
i. 2977 court complexes are equipped with bandwidth speed ranging from 10 Mbps to 100 
Mbps. 
ii. 1.21 cr. cases have been filed through the e-filing platform. 
iii.  The e-payments system has processed transactions for court -fee worth Rs. 1,594 crore 
and fine worth Rs. 97 crore. 

iv. Case Information System (CIS) 4.0 has been implemented in all courts, with enhanced 
privacy safeguards and integration with national platforms such as NJDG, e -filing, 
virtual courts and Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS). 
v. More than 35.57 lakh FIRs and 38.36 lakh Chargesheet have been received by the courts 
(CIS 4.0) digitally from CCTNS. 
vi. The eSummons system has been introduced for electronic delivery of summons through 
email. 
vii. Through the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), litigants can access case information 
in respect of over 32.46 crore cases and over 39.79 crore orders/judgments. 
viii. The courts have conducted over 4.15 cr. hearings through video conferencing, facilitating 
remote hearings of undertrials, witnesses and lawyers.  
ix. Over 734 crore pages of court records including legacy records have been digitized across 
courts.  
x. To safely and permanently store court records, a robust digital vault “Judicial Digital 
Trustworthy Repository” has been developed.  
xi. The JustIS app (22,534 downloads) helps the judges to effectively organise and monitor 
judicial work. 
xii. 31 Virtual Courts have been established to enable online adjudication of traffic challans. 
xiii. 2,515 e-Sewa Kendras are functional across High Courts and District Courts to provide 
citizen centric services to lawyers and litigants. 
xiv. An AI based software tool called Legal Research Analysis Assistant [LegRAA] has been 
developed to aid judges in legal research and document analysis.  
xv. The S3WaaS platform hosts 730 Courts websites, ensuring secure and accessible web 
infrastructure.  
 
The details of funds released to various High Courts, as recommended by e -Committee, 
Supreme Court of India, under the eCourts Project during the last three years, are at 
Annexure.  
 
In addition, several steps taken by the Government to reduce judicial delays and improve 
access to justice through technology and judicial reforms are as under: 
 
i. Under the Centrally Sponsored Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) Scheme, for the 
expeditious disposal of pending cases of Rape and POCSO Act, 775 Fast Track 
Special Courts (FTSCs) including 398 exclusive POCSO (ePOCSO) Courts are 
functional across 29 States/UTs and have collectively disposed of 3,87,481 cases.  
ii. Arrears Committees have been set up in all 25 High Courts and the District Courts to 
clear cases pending for more than five years.   
iii. The Government has also enacted New Criminal Laws 2023, The Negotiable 
Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, The Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 
2018

940.    DR. VINOD KUMAR BIND:

Will the Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS be pleased to state:

(a) the progress made under the Sagarmala Programme in terms of port modernisation, 
new port development and coastal economic zone projects; 
(b) the steps taken to enhance port capacity, efficiency, and reduce turnaround time at 
major and non-major ports;  
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any initiatives to improve last-mile 
connectivity through road, rail and inland waterways and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether any projects relating to port-led development, fishing harbours, coastal 
infrastructure, coastal community development or last-mile connectivity have been 
sanctioned or implemented under the Sagarmala programme in Andhra Pradesh and if 
so, the details thereof indicating the funds allocated and the present status of 
implementation, district-wise including Bapatla district? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS 
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL) 
 (a)       Sagarmala scheme is a central sector scheme of Ministry of Ports, Shipping and 
Waterways (MoPSW) with the target to promote port-led development in the country. 
Under this scheme, MoPSW provides financial assistance for the projects under 5 pillars 

namely, port modernization, port connectivity, port-led industrialization, coastal 
community development, and coastal shipping & inland water transport. The pillar wise 
progress of the projects funded under Sagarmala scheme is available at Annexure-I.  
 (b)       Government has taken several measures to enhance port capacity, improve 
operational efficiency, and reduce vessel turnaround time at major ports. Infrastructure 
development and capacity augmentation is a continuous process and includes 
construction of new berths and terminals, mechanization, modernization and optimization 
of existing berths and terminals, capital dredging to deepen drafts for accommodating 
larger vessels, development of road and rail connectivity, and creation of supporting 
infrastructure such as parking plazas. Further, port processes have been streamlined with 
the implementation of One Nation One Port Process (ONOP) to improve operational 
efficiency and reduce vessel turnaround time. As a result of these initiatives, the cargo 
handling capacity of the Major and Other than Major Ports (OTMP) has increased to 2,818 
Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) as on March 2026 from ~1,400 MTPA in 2013-14. 
(c)       One of the objectives of Sagarmala programme is better port connectivity, efficient 
cargo movement between ports and their respective hinterland to minimize overall 
logistics cost. Sagarmala programme has a dedicated pillar of port connectivity which 
focuses on the last mile and immediate hinterland connectivity of the ports via road, rail 
and inland waterways. Further, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade 
(DPIIT) has undertaken a comprehensive assessment of port connectivity and prepared 
a Comprehensive Port Connectivity Plan (CPCP) in 2022 by reviewing connectivity of the 
operational ports and identified the ports which needed improvement of road and/ or rail 
connectivity with nearby economic hubs. 
Subsequently, MoPSW in consultation with Ministry of Road, Transport and 
Highways and Ministry of Railways has identified a total of 294 rail and road connectivity 
projects, out of which, 84 projects (63 Rail and 21 Road) have been completed, 66 
projects (27 Rail and 39 Road) are under implementation, and a total of 144 projects (42 
Rail and 102 Road) are under planning stage. The connectivity projects within the port 
limits are taken up by the Port Authorities and beyond the port limits are taken up by 
Ministries like MoR, MoRTH or State Governments. 
  
As regard to inland waterway connectivity projects, details of projects completed 
by Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) on National Waterways (NW) are as under:  
i. 3 Multi Modal Terminals (MMTs) and 01 intermodal terminal on NW 1 
ii. 1 MMT and 3 IWT terminals on NW 2   
iii. 9 IWT terminals on NW 3;  
iv. 02 Roll-on/Roll-off (Ro-Ro) terminals in Ernakulam  
v. 01 Ro-Ro terminal on NW 4 
  

(d)       The MoPSW has sanctioned financial assistance of ₹ 272 crore to 9 projects worth 
₹ 1,286 crore under Sagarmala scheme in the state of Andhra Pradesh and the details of 
these projects are available at Annexure-II. These projects are related to Ro-Pax and 
passe

†941. Dr. Rajkumar Sangwan:

Drug Quality and Production Promotion Scheme during the last seven years; 
(b) whether the Government has established any action plan or set targets to promote the export of 
traditional medicines and health products through the Drug Quality and Production Promotion 
Scheme, if so, the achievements made during the last seven years; 
(c) whether the Government has taken any measures for effective quality control and safety 
monitoring of AYUSH medicines; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
(a) & (b) Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta 
evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY)  since 2021-22 with total budget outlay of Rs. 
122.00 crores for five years. The components of scheme are as follows: - 
 
i. Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to 
achieve higher standards. 
ii. Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H drugs including surveillance of misleading advertisements. 
iii. Strengthening of Central and State regulatory frameworks including Technical Human 
Resource & Capacity Building programs for Ayush drugs. 
iv. Support for development of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & 
materials in collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Control of India 
(QCI) and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial R&D centers. 

 
2 
 
   
 The scheme has inter alia one of the component to strengthen and up -grade the Ayush 
Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories (DTLs) to achieve higher standards like WHO -GMP 
and NABL, which ease the exports of Ayush drugs. Till date, 18 Ayush pharmacies and 07 Ayush 
DTLs have been supported financially under this scheme across the country. An amount of Rs. 
40.13 crore has been sanctioned as Grant -in-Aid to these pharmacies and DTLs.  The State/UT-
wise details of fund released for the upgradation of Ayush pharmacies and Drug Testing 
Laboratories (DTLs) under the AOGUSY scheme till date are attached at Annexure. 
 
         Further, to s trengthen Central and State regulatory frameworks, Ayush vertical in C entral 
Drugs Standards Control Organization (CD SCO) and State Ayush Directorate/State Drug 
Controller of Ayush drugs are financially supported under AOGUSY Scheme for conducting 
training and capacity building programs.  
 
(c) & (d) The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory 
provisions for Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homoeopathy (ASSU&H) drugs.  It is 
mandatory for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed requirements for licensing of 
manufacturing units & medicines including proof of safety & effectiveness, compliance with the 
Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T and Schedule M of the Drugs Rules, 
1945 for Ayurvedic, Siddha, Sowa-rigpa, Unani and Homeopathy drugs respectively and to follow 
the quality standards of drugs as prescribed in the respective pharmacopoeia. 
             
 Drug Inspectors collect medicine samples regularly from manufacturing firms or retail 
shops within their jurisdiction and send them to Drug Testing Laboratory under Drug Control 
department for quality testing and if any sample is found to be ‘Not of Standard Quality’, 
appropriate action is initiated such as preventing the sale of the medicines from the market and 
appropriate legal actions as per Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules made thereunder. There 
are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in Stat e/UTs for testing of the Legal Samples drawn 
by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs. 
  
 The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a 
subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial standards and 
formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official compendia for determining 
their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these standards is mandatory under the Drugs 
and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. PCIM&H also functions as the Appellate 
Drug Testing Laboratory for Ayush drugs and conducts regular capacity-building programmes for 
Drug Regulatory Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other stakeholders on standardization, quality 
control, and testing methodologies to strengthen the quality assurance system for Ayush drugs.

942. Shri Malaiyarasan D:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the total number of functional Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) across the country, 
State/UTwise, including Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu;  
(b) the details of medicines made available through the said Kendras and their price comparison 
with branded alternatives, along with the mechanism for quality assurance;  
(c) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under the scheme during the last three 
financial years and the current year, year-wise;  
(d) whether the Government has assessed the accessibility of the said Kendras in rural, remote 
and urban slum areas and if so, the findings thereof;  
(e) the steps taken to ensure uninterrupted supply of essential medicines and to address 
complaints regarding availability and stock-outs at the said Kendras; and  
(f) whether the Government proposes to expand the network of JAKs and increase public 
awareness about generic medicines, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA) 
 
(a).  Under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana scheme, a total of 20,149 Jan 
Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across the country till 30.06.2026 of which 1631 
JAKs have been opened in the State of Tamil Nadu including 74 JAKs (62 JAKs in Salem & 
12 JAKs in Kallakurichi district) in the Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency. The State -wise 
/Union Territory-wise number of JAKs opened across the country is at Annexure.  
 
(b). The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Yojna has 2,110 
medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, covering all major therapeutic 
groups, such as cardiovascular, anti -cancer, anti -diabetic, anti -infectives, anti -allergic and 
gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals. Medicines are available under PMBJP product 
basket at rates that are about 50% to 80% cheaper than those of branded medicines. 
 
With a view to ensure quality of medicines available at JAKs so that health of patients is 
not compromised, effective mechanisms have been put in place to ensure continuous 
inspection, testing and standardisation, viz.:  
(i) Supply only from WHO Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) certified plants: Only 
WHO-GMP compliant units are eligible for supply. 

(ii) Distribution only after 100% pre -testing of all medicine batches: Random testing of 
100% batches supplied at PMBI’s warehouses, and medicines are dispatched for supply 
to JAKs only after successful quality test. 
(iii)Testing only at labs compliant with Good Laboratory Practices (GLP): Samples are 
tested only at labs accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and 
Calibration Laboratories  (NABL) and, in addition, assessed by PMBI for GLP 
compliance.

funds allocated and utilised during the last three years are as under:

UNIVERSAL IMMUNIZATION PROGRAMME
943. SMT. APARAJITASARANGI:
SHRI CHA VDAVINOD LAKHAMSHI:
SHRI RAMESH AWASTHI:
SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA:
SHRI PARIMALSUKLABAIDYA:
SHRI CHANDRA PRAKASH JOSH:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the progress made so far in the implementation of the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)
and the recent initiatives taken to introduce new vaccines in the country, State/UT-wise, including
Assam;
(b) the measures taken by the Government to improve immunisation in remote, tribal, tea garden and
flood-prone areas of Assam;
(c) the details of the key experiences gained from the management of the COVID-19 pandemic along
with the steps taken by the Government to strengthen pandemic preparedness, disease surveillance and
rapid response systems in the country, including Assam;
(d) the measures taken by the Union Government for the capacity building of healthcare workers and
strengthening of oxygen infrastructure and critical care facilities in the country, including Assam; and
(e) whether digital health platforms and data analytics are being effectively used for disease
surveillance, vaccination tracking and public health emergency response in the country and if so, the
details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)
(a) The Full Immunization coverage for the last 3 years in the country and State/UT wise including
Assam is given in Annexure 1. The Nationwide HPV vaccination campaign was launched on 28th
February 2026 for identified and eligible beneficiary girls aged 14 years across all 36 States and Union
Territories.
The HPV vaccine is delivered free of cost at designated government health facilities, including
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs- Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centers (CHCs), Sub
-District Hospitals (SDH)/District Hospitals (DHs) & Government Medical Colleges (GMCs).
Awareness generation is promoted through IEC materials such as radio jingles, posters, banners, myth-
busting digital content and social media platforms to ensure high vaccine uptake among girls
particularly in rural, tribal, and urban slum areas. Training on HPV vaccination has been completed for
medical and paramedical staff across all 36 States/UTs in the country.
(b) As informed by the Government of Assam, Assam Government has taken special measures to
reach the undeserved and hard-to-reach areas (HRA); tea garden, flood prone area, hilly terrain as well
as urban slum population. Activity strengthened by hiring Vehicle, boat and ANM for improving

immunization coverage. The Immunization services are also provided to pregnant women and children
in riverine areas by Boat Clinics.
(c) and (d) The Ministry of Health and family Welfare GoI, has strengthened pandemic preparedness ,
disease surveillance, rapid response systems as given below:
 Pradhan Mantri - Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) launched in 2021
strengthens public health infrastructure at the primary and secondary levels of care; enhance
capacity for disease surveillance, diagnostics, and research for emerging and re-emerging diseases;
and develop a resilient health system capable of responding effectively to public health
emergencies.
 Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) strengthened for carrying out disease
surveillance activities, has a decentralized system of response through trained multi-disciplinary
Rapid Response Teams (RRTs).
 Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) established a network of more than 160 Virus
Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) for laboratory based diagnosis of pathogens.
 The Integrated Training is a single, structured, and competency-driven framework for Medical
Officers (MO), Staff Nurses (SN), Community Health Officers (CHO), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives
(ANM) and ASHAs (and ASHA Facilitators).
 Oxygen cylinders, oxygen concentrators & Liquid Medical Oxygen tanks supplied to the
States/UTs, along with establishment of Pressure Swing Adsorption plants (PSA) plants and
Medical Gas Pipeline Systems in States/UTs.
(e) Digital health platforms effectively used for disease surveillence include Integrated Health
Information Platform (IHIP), Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), Health Management
Information System (HMIS), Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) Portal and National Program for Non
Communicable Disease (NP-NCD) Portal. These portals enable real-time data collection, data analysis,
data visualization and dissemination of epidemiological information to support early detection of
outbreaks. The UWIN platform facilitates digital tracking of the vaccines for all eligible beneficiaries.

of centres set up and measurable outcomes thereof across the country since its 
inception, State-wise and year-wise including Maharashtra and Bihar; 
(b) the manner in which the single Bharat brand has benefited farmers and reduced

(c) the quantum of fertilizers being marketed and distributed at subsidised rates under the

(a) and (b)  Vide notification dated 24th August, 2022, Government of India has decided to 
implement One Nation One Fertilizers (ONOF) by introducing Single Bharat Brand for 
Fertilizers and Logo under Fertilizer subsidy scheme namely “Pradhanmantri Bhartiya 
Janurvarak Pariyojna” (PMBJP). All fertilizers companies viz Public sector, Cooperative 
and Private sector are required to sell subsidized fertilizers under brand name “BHARAT” 
across the country. The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of 
fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands 
manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross 
movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country including the 
States of Maharashtra, Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan. By consolidating branding 
under a single “BHARAT” brand, the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, 
and ensures equitable access to essential nutrients for crops. The mandate of Department 
of Fertilizers is to ensure adequate availability of fertilizers at State level. The distribution 
of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the concerned State Government.  
(c)  Following Steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
uninterrupted, timely and adequate supply of fertilizers across the States/UTs: 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers.  
(ii) On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, D/o Fertilizers allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
(iii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
(iv) Regular Weekly Video Conference is conducted jointly by DA&FW and D/o 
Fertilizers with State Agriculture Officials and corrective actions are taken to dispatch 
fertilizers as indicated by the State Governments. 

 
(v) The distribution of fertilizers within the State is done by the respective State 
Government.

the ongoing Kharif 2026 (from 01.04.2026 to 19.07.2026) season across the States/UTs.

entries.t: Promotion of AYUSH Systems of Medicine
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 946 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
Promotion of AYUSH Systems of Medicine 
 
946. Shri Janardan Singh Sigriwal: 
Will the Minister of AYUSH be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps for the promotion and expansion of AYUSH 
systems of the medicine in the State of Bihar during the last three years and the current year; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the schemes/programmes implemented and funds  
allocated, released and utilised for the promotion of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, 
Siddha and Homoeopathy in Bihar, Stream-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has established, upgraded or supported AYUSH 
hospitals/dispensaries/medical colleges/research Institutions/AYUSH Health and Wellness  
Centres/ Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) in Bihar during the said period; 
(d) if so, the details thereof, district -wise along with the number of AYUSH practitioners,  
teaching faculty and healthcare personnel engaged under such initiatives; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to further strengthen AYUSH infrastructure, education, 
research and healthcare delivery in Bihar and if so, the details thereof including the projects 
proposed, funds earmarked and timelines for implementation? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
(a) & (b) Ministry of Ayush is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Ayush 
Mission (N AM) through State/UT Governments including Bihar  and providing financial 
assistance to them for promotion and expansion of Ayush systems of the medicine in the country 
against their proposals received through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) as per the 
provisions of NAM guidelines. The Mission inter -alia makes provision for the following 
activities: - 
(i) Ayush Health & Wellness Centres now renamed as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush). 
(ii) Co -location of Ayush facilities at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health 
Centres (CHCs) and District Hospitals (DHs). 
(iii) Upgradation of existing standalone Government Ayush Hospitals. 
(iv) Upgradation of existing Government/Panchayat/Government aided Ayush 
Dispensaries/Construction of building for existing Ayush Dispensary (Rented/ dilapidated 
accommodation)/Construction of building to establish new Ayush Dispensary in the area where 
there are no Ayush facilities available. 
(v) Setting up of upto 10/30/50 bedded Integrated Ayush Hospitals. 

(vi) Supply of essential drugs to Government Ayush Hospitals, Government Dispensaries and 
Government/Government aided Teaching Institutional Ayush Hospitals. 
(vii) Ayush Public Health Programmes. 
(viii) Establishment of new Ayush  colleges in the St ates where availability of Ayush  teaching 
institutions is inadequate in Government Sector. 
(ix) Infrastructural development of Ayush Under-Graduate Institutions and Ayush Post-Graduate 
Institutions/ add on PG/ Pharmacy /Para-Medical Course. 
Under, NAM  during last three years, an amount of Rs. 1383.343 Lakhs has been 
sanctioned and released to State Government of Bihar  for implementation of different approved 
activities in the received SAAPs  regarding overall development & promotion of Ayush system 
including Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani Siddha and Homoeopathy as approved . As 
reported by the State Government, they have made expenditure for an amount of Rs 980.388 
Lakhs. There is no provision of stream-wise allocation of funds under NAM.  
(c) to (e ) Public Health being a State subject, the primary responsibility of 
establishment/upgradation of Ayush health facilities and strengthening of Ayush infrastructure, 
education, research &  healthcare delivery  in Bihar lies with respective State Government.   
However, under NAM , there are  provision of providing financial assistance to the State/UT 
Governments for the establishment of 50/30/10 bedded Integrated Ayush H ospitals, upgradation 
of existing Ayush Hospitals, establishment of New Ayush education institute and upgradation of 
existing Ayush Educational Institutes. State/UT Governments may avail financial assistance for 
these by submitting suitable proposal through SAAP as per the provisions of NAM guidelines. 
As per the proposals received from State Government through SAAPs , 294 AAM (Ayush) have 
been supported for operationalisation and 10 Integrated Ayush Hospitals have been approved for 
establishment. The district -wise details of AAM  (Ayush) and approved IAHs  is furnished at 
Annexure.  
 As Public Health is  a State subject, the primary responsibility for engagement of Ayush 
practitioners, teaching faculty and healthcare personnel  in Bihar comes under the purview of 
respective State Government. No such data is being maintained at Central level.

Honorarium to AWWs and AWHs 
†947. Shri Amra Ram:         
 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Helpers (AWHs) working in the country and 
the number of vacant posts, State -wise, the total amount of honorarium being given monthly to 
said workers and the ratio of Central and State Government share in the s aid honorarium, State-
wise; and  
  
(b) whether the Government proposes to make the honorarium of the said workers equal to the 
minimum wage, if so, the timeline thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD  
DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
(a) & (b)   State-wise details of field functionaries is available on Poshan Tracker and can be 
accessed at: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. 
Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) are honorary workers drawn from 
the local community who voluntarily come forward to render their services in the area of child 
care and development to help the local community for which they are paid ho norarium. This 
honorarium is increased from time to time. From 1 st October, 2018, Government of India has 
enhanced the honorarium of AWWs at Anganwadi centres (AWCs) from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.4,500/- 
per month and AWHs from Rs.1,500/ - to Rs.2,250/- per month as per cost sharing ratio which is 
as under:

2 North Eastern and Himalayan States 90 10

In addition, States and UTs are also paying additional monetary incentives and top ups to these 
functionaries from their own resources which vary from State to State. Details of additional top 
ups provided by States and UTs are at Annexure.  
Besides, performance linked incentive of Rs.500/- per month is provided to AWWs and Rs.250/- 
per month to AWHs. 
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, AWWs have been technologically 
empowered with the provision of smartphones for efficient monitoring and delivery of services. 
Poshan Tracker which is a mobile phone application that has digitized physical reg isters used by 
Anganwadi workers. This improves the quality of their work while simultaneously enabling them 
for real-time monitoring of all activities going on in the Anganwadis.   
To incentivize and encourage the AWWs and AWHs, various initiatives have been undertaken 
including the following: 
(i)  Promotion: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, promotional opportunities 
for AWWs and AWHs have been enhanced. 50% posts of AWWs are to be filled by AWHs with 
5 years of experience and 50% posts of Supervisors are to be filled by promotion  of AWWs with 
5 years of experience subject to fulfilment of other criteria. 
(ii)  Leave: 20 days’ annual leave and paid maternity absence of 180 days and paid absence on 
abortion/ miscarriage once for 45 days. 
(iii)  State Governments and UT Administrations have been requested to encourage eligible 
AWWs and AWHs to get  themselves enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Mandhan 
(PM-SYM) Pension Scheme, which is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for  the 
unorganized sector in the country to ensure old age protection. 
(iv)  Social Security Insurance Schemes: Insurance benefits have been provided to AWWs and 
AWHs under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) for life cover worth Rs.2.00 
lakh (covers life risk, death due to any reason) in the age group of 18 to 50 years and under Pradhan 
Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana for accidental cover of Rs.2.00 Lakh (accidental death and 
permanent full disability) /Rs.1.00 Lakh (partial but permanent disability) in the age group of 18-
59 years. 
(v)  Retirement date: States and UTs have been requested to adopt a uniform retirement date i.e 
30th April of each year with respect to AWWs and AWHs to ensure proper human resource 
planning. 

(vi)  Annual Healthcare coverage of Rs. 5 Lakhs under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan 
Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) to all AWWs and AWHs in pursuance to budget announcement in 
FY 2024-25.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

INDIGENOUS PRODUCTION OF CRITICAL CHEMICAL MATERIALS 
  
948. SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY:  
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS, be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether Government is aware that imports of chemical materials and products increased 
by 44.4 per cent year-on-year during April-December, 2025; 
  
(b) the measures taken by the Gove rnment to promote indigenous production of critical 
chemical inputs and intermediates to reduce dependence on import while maintaining global 
competitiveness; 
  
(c) whether any assessment has been conducted by the Government regarding the potential for 
domestic chemical manufacturers to integrate into global value chains for pharmaceutical, 
electronics and renewable energy sectors, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
  
ANSWER 
  
                  THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
                  (SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)  
  
(a):    As per the data available on the website of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry, imports of major chemical materials and products increased from 
₹4,70,570.43 Crore during April –December 2024 to ₹5,21,964.05 Crore during April –
December 2025, registering an increase of 10.92 per cent. 
  

(b):      The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals has taken the following initiatives 
to promote indigenous production  of critical chemical inputs and intermediates to reduce 
import dependency while maintaining global competitiveness: 
  
Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIR): 
  
The Department had notified the Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemical Investment Region 
(PCPIR) Policy. PCPIRs are conceptualized as cluster -based model of Development with 
common infrastructure and support services. Three PCPIRs have been set up at Dahej  
(Gujarat), Vishakhapatnam –Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh) and Paradeep (Odisha). Currently, 
2,246 chemical units are functional in these PCPIRs having a cumulative investment of Rs. 
3,49,192 Crore and these regions have generated employment of 3.7 lakh persons. 
Plastic Park Scheme:  
The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) implements the Scheme for Setting 
up of Plastic Parks. The Scheme promotes setting up of need-based Plastic Parks with requisite 
state-of-the-art infrastructure and enabling commo n facilities. The objective is to consolidate 
and synergize the capacities of downstream plastic processing industry to help increase 
investment, production and export in the sector as well as generate employment. Under the 
Scheme, the Government of India provides grant funding up to 50% of the project cost to the 
State Government subject to a ceiling of Rs. 40 Crore per project. In accordance with the 
Scheme Guidelines, 10 Plastic Parks that have been approved are at different stages of 
implementation. 
Centres of Excellence (CoEs):  
The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals has implemented a Scheme for setting up of 
Centres of Excellence. The objective is to provide grants -in-aid to educational and research 
institutions to improve existing technology a nd promote development of new applications of 
polymers and plastics. In 2024, the Scheme was also extended to include research related to 
Chemicals. The emphasis of the Scheme is on modernization and upgradation of existing 
manufacturing processes as well as improving the quality of products. Under the Scheme, the 
Government of India provides financial support up to 50 per cent of the total project cost subject 
to an upper limit of Rs. 5 Crore. 18 CoEs have been approved under the Scheme. 
Chemical Promotion and Development Scheme (CPDS): 
The Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals is also implementing the Chemical Promotion 
and Development Scheme (CPDS) to attract investment and facilitate growth and development 
of Chemicals and Petrochemicals Industry by dissemination of knowledge through conduct of 
seminars, conferences, exhibitions, etc. in different sub sectors of the industry such as 
Agrochemicals, Dyes and Pigments, Chlor-Alkali, Plastics and Petrochemicals.  

These events promote Indian industry and tr ade, attract foreign investment, encourage R&D 
for indigenization of technologies, improve skills and support sustainability initiatives for 
comprehensive development of the sector.

Participation in Global Value Chains," has assessed the potential for integrating India's

IMPACT OF NEET-BASED ADMISSIONS ON MEDICAL SEATS
950. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the impact of NEET-based admissions on
availability of medical seats for students from rural and regional language backgrounds;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Government has received any requests from States for greater flexibility in
admissions to Government medical colleges and if so, the details thereof;
(d) the number of MBBS seats added in Government medical colleges during the last five

(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure fair, transparent and accessible medical
admissions across the country?

NEET (UG) serves as the common entrance examination for admission to MBBS/ BDS/
BAMS/ BSMS/ BUMS/ BHMS and other Under-Graduate medical courses in

Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)   whether the Government has expanded One Stop Centre coverage with enhanced staffing 
norms reflecting district -wise caseload variations for trauma support to women, if so, details 
thereof; 
  
(b)   the details of the measures being undertaken to integrate police personnel and legal aid 
services within centres eliminating requirement for victims to narrate trauma at multiple locations; 
  
(c)   whether structured migration support functions providing transitional accommodation and 
city orientation services for women migrating independently for employment have been piloted, 
if so, details thereof; 
  
(d)   the details of the rehabilitation frameworks established for ensuring that women receive 
comprehensive post-crisis support including livelihood linkages and sustained monitoring after 
leaving centres; and 
  
(e)   the manner in which reformed One Stop Centre architecture transforms crisis -response 
institutions into preventive platforms supporting safe migration and sustained workforce 
participation under Mission Shakti framework? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
  
(a) to (e):   One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical under the umbrella 
Mission Shakti. It provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof  to 
women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces all across the 
country.  So far, 1,033 One Stop Centres (OSCs) have been approved across the country.  Out of 
which, 985 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country and since inception, 

i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30 th June, 2026, over 15.20 lakh women have been assisted in the country. 
The Central Government provides 100% financial assistance to States/ UTs for appointment/hiring 
13 manpower resources including 1 Centre Administrator, 2 Case Workers, 1 Psycho -social 
Counsellor, 1 Para Legal Personnel/ Lawyer, 1 Para Medical Personnel at each OSC   with a 
provision of flexibility in the staffing composition based on local needs and operational 
feasibility.  The overall implementation of the OSC scheme lies with the State Governments and 
UT Administrations.  
  To strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services, OSCs have been 
integrated with the Women Helpline (WHL), and so far, 657 OSCs have been integrated. Through 
this integration, women can be referred to appropriate services in a timely and coordinated manner. 
Further, the Women Helpline has been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System 
(ERSS-112), Child Helpline (1098) and other relevant service delivery mechanisms to facilitate 
prompt emergency response and effective inter-agency coordination. In addition, OSCs have also 
been integrated with Shakti Sadan to enable referral of women requiring long -term institutional 
support, rehabilitation and safe accommodation, thereby ensuring a continuum of care under the 
Mission Shakti framework. 
  Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile schemes of ‘Swadhar Greh’ – Home for 
women in difficult circumstances and ‘Ujjawala’ - Home for women rescued from Trafficking, 
have been merged and are now known as ‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’, which is an Integr ated Relief 
and Rehabilitation Home for women in distressful situations including trafficked women.  It aims 
at creating a safe and enabling environment for the women in such difficult situations, to enable 
them to overcome the adverse circumstances. 
  Under Shakti Sadan Scheme, the residents of Shakti Sadan are provided with shelter, food, 
clothing, counselling, primary health facilities and other daily requirements. The residents also to 
be provided vocational training, facility for opening of bank accounts, social security benefits etc. 
in convergence with the relevant departments. Further, arrangement is made by the implementing 
organization for providing vocational training/ skill development classes to the women through 
the Vocational Training Insti tutes recognized by the Directorate General of Employment and 
Training under the Ministry of Labour and Employment/ Training Partners of National Skill 
Development Council (NSDC). Training and examination fee, if not provided under any other 
scheme/ programmes of the Central/ State Government, would be reimbursed on submission of 
the certificate i ssued by the vocational training institute on successful completion of training. 
Micro Credit will be facilitated through SIDBI, Mudra and other relevant schemes of Central/State 
government in case residents want to start small-scale industry/ business.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026
CITIZENS ENROLLMENT UNDER ABDM
958. SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S:
Will the Minister of HEALTH and FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of citizens enrolled under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in the
country so far, State-wise, particularly in Arani Lok Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu;
(b) the number of hospitals, clinics and health providers registered under ABDM and their
geographical distribution;
(c) whether the Government has evaluated the impact of ABDM on patient care, access to
healthcare services and efficiency of health services delivery in the country especially in rural
areas, if so, the details thereof;
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure data security, privacy and interoperability of health
records under ABDM; and
(e) the measures adopted by the Government to integrate ABDM with existing public health
programmes, insurance schemes and State health databases?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (e): As of 20th July 2026, under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), 94.87 crore
ABHAs have been created across the country, including 2.57 crore in Tamil Nadu. While creating
ABHAs, Lok Sabha constituency details are not captured. As of 20th July 2026, 17,81,231 ( 10,25,823
in Tiruvannamalai District and 7,55,408 in Viluppuram District) ABHA registrations has been registered
in the Arani Lok Sabha constituency of Tamil Nadu:
Under ABDM, Health Facility Registry (HFR) has been created which includes verified healthcare
facilities such hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, blood banks etc. As of 20th July 2026, 5.36 lakh facilities
are registered on the HFR. Similarly, the Healthcare Professionals Registry is a registry of verified
healthcare professionals. As of 20th July 2026, 10.09 lakh healthcare professionals are registered on the
HPR. The state-wise and district-wise distribution, is available on the real-time ABDM dashboard at
https://dashboard.abdm.gov.in/

A third-party evaluation study of the ABDM was conducted between June-August 2025. The key
findings of the evaluation study are highlighted below
● ABDM has reduced waiting times, enabled cost savings, and improved service access,
particularly benefiting women and underserved populations.
● Considering the well-structured strategic foundation, robust digital infrastructure rollout, and
effective stakeholder engagement across public and private sectors, ABDM has brought in
efficiency in the health service delivery ecosystem.
● Unified Health Interface (UHI) serves as a key digital gateway under ABDM, facilitating
seamless discovery and delivery of health services and significantly enhancing accessibility,
convenience, and reach of healthcare services for citizens
● ABDM has shown impact by enhancing healthcare efficiency, accessibility, and affordability,
especially for underserved groups. Its interoperable infrastructure and cross-sectoral
collaborations have driven systemic shifts, through broader integration and measurable health
outcomes which are key to sustaining long term success
‘Privacy by Design’ is one of the key guiding principles of ABDM and there is no centralised repository
of health data. ABDM facilitates secure data exchange between the intended stakeholders on the ABDM
network after the patient’s consent. Also, before integrating with ABDM, digital health applications are
validated in a Sandbox environment, and they also undergo security audits like WASA (Web
Application Security Audit) to ensure data security.
ABDM enables interoperability by establishing common health data standards and developing registries
for individuals, health facilities, healthcare professionals, and other necessary components. This allows
various digital health systems across both public and private healthcare ecosystems to exchange data
across healthcare providers, even when they use different digital platforms.
Technical support is provided for integration of any digital health solution with ABDM, including
public health programs. Several national and state public health programme platforms including
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), Nikshay, Reproductive and Child Health (RCH), Non-
Communicable Diseases (NCD), Gujarat’s TECHO, Uttar Pradesh’s eKavach, Rajasthan’s Pregnancy,
Child Tracking and Health Services Management (PCTS), Tamil Nadu CMCHIS (Comprehensive
Health Insurance Scheme) are integrated with ABDM.

package include:

shipbuilding force in line with vision contained in Maritime India Vision 2030 and 
Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 documents.
